title: INTEGRAL TECHNOLOGIES INC
text: EX-10.2 6 ex_1023813.htm EXHIBIT 10.2 ex_1023813.htm Exhibit 10.2 EXECUTIVE SERVICES AGREEMENT This EXECUTIVE SERVICES AGREEMENT (the “ Employment Agreement ”) is made and entered into as of November 10, 2026, by and between INTEGRAL TECHNOLOGIES, INC. , a Nevada corporation (the “ Company ”), and Brett Mitchell , an individual (the “ Executive ”) to be engaged for his Executive Services through his consulting entity Sibella Capital Pty Ltd, a Western Australian company (ACN 108 289 818). The Company and the Executive are referred to herein from time to time on a collective basis as the “ Parties ” and each on individual basis as a “ Party .” RECITALS The Company wishes to secure the services of the Executive as Chief Executive Officer of the Company upon the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth, and the Executive wishes to render such services to the Company upon the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth. AGREEMENT NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and obligations set forth herein, the parties agree as follows: 1. Term . Subject to Section 5 of this Agreement, the Executive’s initial term of employment hereunder shall be from the period beginning on the date of this Agreement (the “ Effective Date ”) and ending on the first (1st) anniversary of the Effective Date (the “ Initial Term ”). Thereafter, the Agreement shall be deemed to be automatically extended, upon the same terms and conditions, for successive periods of six months, unless either party provides written notice of its intention not to extend the term at least 90 days prior to the end of the Initial Term or six month extension thereof. The period during which the Executive is employed by the Company hereunder is hereinafter referred to as the “ Employment Term .” 2. Position and Duties . During the Employment Term, the Company shall employ Executive in the position of Chief Executive Officer and in such additional roles as the Board may appoint from time to time. The Executive accepts such employment and shall have such duties and responsibilities as are reasonably assigned, delegated and determined as are customarily assigned to individuals serving in such position and such other duties consistent with the Executive’s title (with such other duties and/or offices in the Company and its affiliates as may be assigned from time to time by the Company, or its Board of Directors and as agreed to by the Executive) and the Executive accepts such employment and agrees to perform such duties. The Executive agrees to devote his full customary business time and energies to the business of the Company and/or its affiliates and subsidiaries to perform his duties hereunder. 3. Place of Performance . The Executive will perform his work duties remotely. However, the Executive shall undertake such occasional travel, within or outside the United States, as is reasonably necessary in the interests of the Company. 4. Compensation . 4.1 Base Salary. The Company shall pay to the Executive a base salary for all services to be rendered by the Executive under this Employment Agreement at the rate of $240,000 plus GST per annum (the applicable amount, the “ Base Salary ”). The Base Salary shall accrue daily on and from the Effective Date and is payable monthly in advance. The Executive will issue an invoice each month from Sibella Capital Pty Ltd for payment of the Base Salary. 4.2 Annual Bonus . Commencing in the calendar year 2026 and each calendar year thereafter during Executive’s employment with the Company, the Executive will be eligible to receive an annual performance bonus in the amount of up to 50% of the Executive’s Base Salary (the “ Annual Bonus ”) as determined by the Board (or a committee thereof) in its sole discretion, which Annual Bonus shall be paid in full within ninety (90) days following each year of employment or in such other intervals as determined by the board of directors of the Company. Any Annual Bonus earned by the Executive pursuant to this Section shall be paid to the Executive in accordance with Company policies, less authorized deductions and required withholding obligations. 4.3 Equity Awards . During the Employment Term, the Executive shall be eligible to receive equity awards as determined by the Board (or a committee thereof) in its sole discretion. The Board shall determine the type, amount, vesting schedule, and other terms and conditions of any such equity awards, which shall be subject to the terms of the Company’s applicable equity incentive plan and the award agreements thereunder. 4.4 Fringe Benefits and Perquisites . During the Employment Term, the Executive shall be entitled to fringe benefits and perquisites consistent with those provided to similarly situated executives of the Company. 4.5 Intentionally omitted . 4.6 Intentionally omitted . 4.7 Business Expenses . The Executive shall be entitled to reimbursement for all reasonable and necessary out-of-pocket business, entertainment, and travel expenses incurred by the Executive in connection with the performance of the Executive’s duties hereunder in accordance with the Company’s expense reimbursement policies and procedures. 4.8 Indemnification . The Company shall indemnify and hold the Executive harmless to the fullest extent applicable to any other officer or director of the Company/to the maximum extent permitted under applicable law and the Company’s bylaws for acts and omissions in the Executive’s capacity as an officer, director, or employee of the Company. 4.9 Intentionally omitted . 5. Termination of Employment . The Employment Term and the Executive’s employment hereunder may be terminated by either the Company or the Executive at any time and for any reason or for no particular reason; provided that, unless otherwise provided herein, either party shall be required to give the other party at least 90 days advance written notice of any termination of the Executive’s employment. Upon termination of the Executive’s employment during the Employment Term, the Executive shall be entitled to the compensation and benefits described in this Section 5 and shall have no further rights to any compensation or any other benefits from the Company or any of its affiliates. 2 5.1 Expiration of the Term, For Cause, or Without Good Reason . (a) The Executive’s employment hereunder may be terminated by the Company for Cause or by the Executive without Good Reason and the Executive shall be entitled to receive: (i) any accrued but unpaid Base Salary which shall be paid within one (1) week following the date of the Executive’s termination in accordance with the Company’s customary payroll procedures; (ii) any unpaid Annual Bonus with respect to any completed fiscal year immediately preceding the date of the Executive’s termination, which shall be paid on the otherwise applicable payment date except to the extent payment is otherwise deferred pursuant to any applicable deferred compensation arrangement; provided that, if the Executive’s employment is terminated by the Company for Cause or the Executive resigns without Good Reason, then any such earned but unpaid Annual Bonus shall be forfeited; (iii) reimbursement for unreimbursed business expenses properly incurred by the Executive, which shall be subject to and paid in accordance with the Company’s expense reimbursement policy; and (iv) intentionally omitted. Items 5.1(a)(i) through 5.1(a)(iv) are referred to herein collectively as the “ Accrued Amounts .” (b) For purposes of this Agreement, “ Cause ” shall mean: (i) the Executive’s failure to comply with any valid and legal directive of the Board or any superior officer of the Company; (ii) the Executive’s engagement in conduct that is illegal, dishonest, or constitutes gross misconduct, or any conduct that is injurious to the Company, its affiliates, or their reputation; (iii) the Executive’s embezzlement, misappropriation, or fraud, whether or not related to the Executive’s employment with the Company; (iv) the Executive’s conviction of, indictment for, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to (A) a crime that constitutes a felony (or state law equivalent), (B) a crime that constitutes a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or fraud, or (C) any crime that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect the Company’s reputation or business; (v) the Executive’s violation of the Company’s written policies or codes of conduct, including policies related to discrimination, harassment, workplace safety, performance of illegal or unethical activities, ethical misconduct, securities trading, or confidentiality; 3 (vi) the Executive’s breach of any obligation under this Agreement, any other written agreement between the Executive and the Company, or any fiduciary duty owed to the Company; (vii) the Executive’s failure to cooperate with any internal or external investigation involving the Company or its affiliates; (viii) the Executive’s gross negligence in the performance of the Executive’s duties; (ix) the Executive’s abuse of alcohol, drugs, or controlled substances that materially interferes with the Executive’s ability to perform the Executive’s duties or that adversely affects the Company’s reputation or business; (x) any act or omission by the Executive that causes material harm to the Company’s business, financial condition, or reputation, or that constitutes a breach of the Executive’s fiduciary duties; (xi) the Executive’s material failure to meet reasonable performance goals or objectives established by the Board after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure, as determined by the Board in its sole discretion; For purposes of this provision, none of the Executive’s acts or failures to act shall be considered “willful” unless the Executive acts, or fails to act, in bad faith or without reasonable belief that the action or failure to act was in the best interests of the Company. Except for a failure, breach, or refusal which, by its nature, cannot reasonably be expected to be cured, the Executive shall have ten (10) business days from the delivery of written notice by the Company within which to cure any acts constituting Cause; provided, however, that no cure period shall be available for any act or omission described in clauses (ii), (iii), (iv), or (vii) above. (c) For purposes of this Agreement, “ Good Reason ” shall mean the occurrence of any of the following, in each case during the Employment Term without the Executive’s prior written consent: (i) a reduction in the Executive’s Base Salary by more than ten percent (10%), other than a reduction that is part of a general reduction in base salaries applicable to all similarly situated executives of the Company; (ii) any material breach by the Company of a material provision of this Agreement that results in demonstrable harm to the Executive; 4 (iii) a material diminution in the Executive’s title or a material and sustained diminution in the Executive’s authority, duties, or responsibilities (other than (A) temporarily while the Executive is physically or mentally incapacitated or as required by applicable law, (B) during any period in which the Executive is failing to perform substantially all of the Executive’s duties, or (C) in connection with the termination of the Executive’s employment for Cause or by the Executive other than for Good Reason). To terminate the Executive’s employment for Good Reason, the Executive must provide written notice to the Company of the existence of the circumstances providing grounds for termination for Good Reason within twenty (20) days of the initial existence of such grounds and the Company must have at least forty-five (45) days from the date on which such notice is provided to cure such circumstances. If the Executive does not terminate the Executive’s employment for Good Reason within fifteen (15) days after the end of the Company’s cure period (or, if earlier, the date the Company notifies the Executive in writing that it will not cure), then the Executive will be deemed to have waived the Executive’s right to terminate for Good Reason with respect to such grounds. 5.2 Without Cause or for Good Reason . The Employment Term and the Executive’s employment hereunder may be terminated by the Executive for Good Reason or by the Company without Cause. In the event of such termination, the Executive shall be entitled to receive the Accrued Amounts, and subject to the Executive’s compliance with Section 6 of this Agreement and the agreements referenced therein and the Executive’s execution, within 30 days following receipt, of a mutual release of claims in favor of the Executive by the Company and by the Executive in favor of the Company, its affiliates and their respective officers and directors in a form provided by the Company (the “ Release ”) that is reasonably acceptable to the Executive, and the Release becoming effective according to its terms, the Executive shall be entitled to receive the following: (a) an amount equal to the greater of (i) the balance of the Executive’s Base Salary that the Executive would have received through the remainder of the Term and (ii) the Executive’s Base Salary for six months, which amount shall be payable in equal monthly installments or otherwise in accordance with the Company’s standard payroll practices; and (b) all unvested securities granted to the Executive under this Agreement shall automatically vest and the treatment of any other outstanding equity awards shall be determined in accordance with the terms of the Plan and the applicable award agreements. 5.3 Death or Disability . (a) The Executive’s employment hereunder shall terminate automatically upon the Executive’s death during the Employment Term, and the Company may terminate the Executive’s employment on account of the Executive’s Disability. (b) If the Executive’s employment is terminated during the Employment Term on account of the Executive’s death or Disability, the Executive (or the Executive’s estate and/or beneficiaries, as the case may be) shall be entitled to receive the following: (i) the Accrued Amounts; and 5 (ii) a lump sum payment equal to the Annual Bonus for the fiscal year, which shall be payable on the later of 5 business days of the Executive’s termination or the ninetieth (90 th ) day following the fiscal year end. Notwithstanding any other provision contained herein, all payments made in connection with the Executive’s Disability shall be provided in a manner which is consistent with federal and state law. (c) For purposes of this Agreement, “ Disability ” shall mean the Executive’s inability, due to physical or mental incapacity, to perform the essential functions of the Executive’s job, with or without reasonable accommodation, for one hundred eighty (180) days out of any three hundred sixty-five (365) day period or one hundred twenty (120) consecutive days. Any question as to the existence of the Executive’s Disability as to which the Executive and the Company cannot agree shall be determined in writing by a qualified independent physician mutually acceptable to the Executive and the Company. The determination of Disability made in writing to the Company and the Executive shall be final and conclusive for all purposes of this Agreement. 5.4 Notice of Termination . Any termination of the Executive’s employment hereunder by the Company or by the Executive during the Employment Term (other than termination pursuant to Section 5.3(a) on account of the Executive’s death) shall be communicated by written notice of termination (“ Notice of Termination ”) to the other party hereto in accordance with Section 17. The Notice of Termination shall specify: (a) the termination provision of this Agreement relied upon; (b) to the extent applicable, the facts and circumstances claimed to provide a basis for termination of the Executive’s employment under the provision so indicated; and (c) the applicable date of termination, which shall be no less than 30 days following the date on which the Notice of Termination is delivered if the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, or no less than 30 days following the date on which the Notice of Termination is delivered if the Executive terminates the Executive’s employment with or without Good Reason; provided that, the Company shall have the option to provide the Executive with a lump sum payment in lieu of such notice. 5.5 Resignation of All Other Positions . Upon termination of the Executive’s employment hereunder for any reason, the Executive shall be deemed to have resigned from all positions that the Executive holds as an officer or member of the Board (or a committee thereof) of the Company or any of its affiliates. 6. Confidential Information and Restrictive Covenants . As a condition of the Executive’s employment with the Company, the Executive shall enter into and abide by the Company’s Employee Confidential Information and Inventions Assignment Agreement or any similar agreement in effect relating to confidentiality. 6 7. Arbitration . Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or related to the Executive’s employment by the Company, or termination of employment, including but not limited to claims arising under or related to this Agreement or any breach of this Agreement, and any alleged violation of federal, state, or local statute, regulation, common law, or public policy, shall be submitted to and decided by binding arbitration with one arbitrator mutually selected by the parties. Arbitration shall be administered exclusively by JAMS and shall be conducted in Washoe County, Nevada, consistent with the rules of JAMS in effect at the time the arbitration is commenced, except as modified by this Agreement. The Parties waive all rights to have their disputes heard or decided by a jury or in a court trial and the right to pursue any class or collective action or representative claims against each other in court, arbitration, or any other proceeding. Any arbitral award determination shall be final and binding upon the parties. 8. Governing Law . This Agreement, for all purposes, shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Nevada without regard to conflicts of law principles. 9. Entire Agreement . Unless specifically provided herein, this Agreement, together with the Employee Confidential Information and Inventions Assignment Agreement, contains all of the understandings and representations between the Executive and the Company pertaining to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous understandings, agreements, representations and warranties, both written and oral, with respect to such subject matter. 10. Modification and Waiver . No provision of this Agreement may be amended or modified unless such amendment or modification is agreed to in writing and signed by the Executive and by at least one other officer of the Company. No waiver by either of the parties of any breach by the other party hereto of any condition or provision of this Agreement to be performed by the other party hereto shall be deemed a waiver of any similar or dissimilar provision or condition at the same or any prior or subsequent time. 11. Severability . Should any provisions of this Agreement be held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provisions hereof, and if such provision or provisions are not modified as provided above, this Agreement shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provisions had not been set forth herein. 12. Captions . Captions and headings of the sections and paragraphs of this Agreement are intended solely for convenience and no provision of this Agreement is to be construed by reference to the caption or heading of any section or paragraph. 13. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in separate counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same instrument. 7 14. Section 409A . 14.1 General Compliance . This Agreement is intended to comply with Section 409A or an exemption thereunder and shall be construed and administered in accordance with such intent. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, payments provided under this Agreement may only be made upon an event and in a manner that complies with Section 409A or an applicable exemption. Any nonqualified deferred compensation payments under this Agreement that may be excluded from Section 409A either as separation pay due to an involuntary separation from service or as a short-term deferral shall be excluded from Section 409A to the maximum extent possible. For purposes of Section 409A, each installment payment provided under this Agreement shall be treated as a separate payment. Any payments to be made under this Agreement upon a termination of employment shall only be made upon a “separation from service” under Section 409A. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company makes no representations that the payments and benefits provided under this Agreement comply with Section 409A, and in no event shall the Company be liable for all or any portion of any taxes, penalties, interest, or other expenses that may be incurred by the Executive on account of non-compliance with Section 409A. 14.2 Specified Employees . Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, if any payment or benefit provided to the Executive in connection with the Executive’s termination of employment is determined to constitute “nonqualified deferred compensation” within the meaning of Section 409A and the Executive is determined to be a “specified employee” as defined in Section 409A(a)(2)(b)(i), then such payment or benefit shall not be paid until the first payroll date to occur following the six-month anniversary of the date of the Executive’s termination or, if earlier, on the Executive’s death (the “ Specified Employee Payment Date ”). The aggregate of any payments that would otherwise have been paid before the Specified Employee Payment Date and interest on such amounts calculated based on the applicable federal rate published by the Internal Revenue Service for the month in which the Executive’s separation from service occurs shall be paid to the Executive in a lump sum on the Specified Employee Payment Date and thereafter, any remaining payments shall be paid without delay in accordance with their original schedule. 14.3 Reimbursements . To the extent required by Section 409A, each reimbursement or in-kind benefit provided under this Agreement shall be provided in accordance with the following: (a) the amount of expenses eligible for reimbursement, or in-kind benefits provided, during each calendar year cannot affect the expenses eligible for reimbursement, or in-kind benefits to be provided, in any other calendar year; (b) any reimbursement of an eligible expense shall be paid to the Executive on or before the last day of the calendar year following the calendar year in which the expense was incurred; and (c) any right to reimbursements or in-kind benefits under this Agreement shall not be subject to liquidation or exchange for another benefit. 15. Successors and Assigns . This Agreement is personal to the Executive and shall not be assigned by the Executive. Any purported assignment by the Executive shall be null and void from the initial date of the purported assignment. The Company may assign this Agreement to any successor or assign (whether direct or indirect, by purchase, merger, consolidation, or otherwise) to all or substantially all of the business or assets of the Company. This Agreement shall inure to the benefit of the Company and permitted successors and assigns. 8 16. Notice . Any notice or other communication required or which may be given hereunder shall be in writing and shall be delivered personally, telecopied, telegraphed or telexed, or sent by certified, registered or express mail, postage prepaid, or emailed to the Parties at the addresses specified on the signature page hereto, or at such other addresses as shall be specified by the parties by like notice, and shall be deemed given so long as such provides a receipt of delivery, when so delivered personally, telecopied, telegraphed or telexed, mailed, or emailed. 17. Representations of the Executive . The Executive represents and warrants to the Company that the Executive’s acceptance of employment with the Company and the performance of the Executive’s duties hereunder will not (a) conflict with or result in a violation of, a breach of, or a default under any contract, agreement, or understanding to which the Executive is a party or is otherwise bound or (b) violate any non-solicitation, non-competition, or other similar covenant or agreement of a prior employer or third-party. 18. Withholding . The Company shall have the right to withhold from any amount payable hereunder any Federal, state, and local taxes in order for the Company to satisfy any withholding tax obligation it may have under any applicable law or regulation. 19. Survival . Upon the expiration or other termination of this Agreement, the respective rights and obligations of the parties hereto shall survive such expiration or other termination to the extent necessary to carry out the intentions of the parties under this Agreement. 20. Acknowledgement of Full Understanding . THE EXECUTIVE ACKNOWLEDGES AND AGREES THAT THE EXECUTIVE HAS FULLY READ, UNDERSTANDS AND VOLUNTARILY ENTERS INTO THIS AGREEMENT. THE EXECUTIVE ACKNOWLEDGES AND AGREES THAT THE EXECUTIVE HAS HAD AN OPPORTUNITY TO ASK QUESTIONS AND CONSULT WITH AN ATTORNEY OF THE EXECUTIVE’S CHOICE BEFORE SIGNING THIS AGREEMENT. [SIGNATURE PAGE FOLLOWS] 9 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Employment Agreement as of the date first above written. COMPANY: INTEGRAL TECHNOLOGIES, INC. By: Name: Title: Address: Email: Sibella Capital Pty Ltd ACN 108 289 818 EXECUTIVE: Brett Mitchell Director Address: 3 Torrens Court Cottesloe WA 6011 Email: brett@sibellax.com.au 10

title: INTEGRAL TECHNOLOGIES INC
text: EX-10.3 7 ex_1024200.htm EXHIBIT 10.3 ex_1024200.htm Exhibit 10.3 Chief Operating Officer – Services Consulting Agreement This Services Consulting Agreement ("Agreement") is made by and between Integral Technologies, Inc. and Lyndsey Wright (“Contractor”). Recitals A. The Company conducts mineral exploration in the United States of America and elsewhere and wishes to engage Contractor to provide services to the Company. B. Contractor desires to enter into this Agreement for the provision of services to the Company. Now, therefore, in consideration of their mutual promises the parties agree: 1. Contractor's Obligation . Contractor shall have the following obligations: 1.1 General Obligations . Contractor will act as the Company’s Chief Operating Officer, whose responsibilities shall include provision of administrative, consulting, management and operations services. 1.2 Specific Obligations . During Contractor’s engagement, Contractor shall have the following obligations: Contractor will report to the Chief Executive Officer, Brett Mitchell, and will be responsible for supporting the management, administration, operation, advancement, and promotion of the Company and its mineral assets. The role may include, without limitation, general administration, accounting and financial management, monthly financial reporting to the Board, expense and invoice tracking, document management, implement procedures to streamline efficiencies, project coordination, landman work, stakeholder liaison, contractor and consultant coordination, land and mineral asset administration, due diligence, agreement review, and commercial support. Contractor will assist with managing the Company’s mineral claims, leases, joint ventures, land positions, optioned assets, and related obligations to ensure the Company’s assets remain in good standing, including tracking and coordinating payment of claim fees, rent, lease payments, option payments, annual payments filings, royalty related payments, renewals, and other property-related obligations. 1 The role may also include reviewing, summarizing, assisting with negotiation of, and managing compliance with land access agreements, mineral leases, option agreements, joint venture agreements, confidentiality agreements, consulting agreements, service agreements, and other legal or commercial agreements. Contractor will liaise with claim staking companies, landmen, geological service providers, accountants, consultants, contractors, laboratories, legal advisors, landowners, government agencies, investors, potential partners, and other stakeholders as required. Contractor will support the promotion and commercialization of the Company’s assets, including reviewing and improving of presentations, project summaries, data rooms, due diligence materials, investor or partner communications, transaction support, and related business development activities. The Company shall provide Contractor with support as required from the Company’s geology team. Contractor will perform such other duties as may reasonably be required by the Company from time to time, consistent with the needs of the Company’s mineral exploration and project generation business. 1.2.1 Best Effort . Contractor shall perform to the best of Contractor's ability all duties assigned to Contractor by the Company and carry out the Company’s policies and directions. 1.2.2 Exclusivity . While performing contract services for the Company on the Company’s properties and prospects, Contractor shall not provide like services on such properties and prospects for any other party than the Company. 1.2.3 Company Fully Advised . While engaged by the Company, Contractor shall keep the Company advised of Contractor's proposed plans, travel and work for the Company. 1.2.4 Preserve Company Assets . Contractor shall care for and preserve the assets of the Company provided to Contractor and return the same to the Company at or before the termination of this Agreement in good and working condition. 1.2.5 Delegation of Duties . Contractor shall not delegate any of Contractor’s duties under this Agreement without the Company's prior written approval. 1.2.6 Observe Applicable Laws . Contractor shall perform the contract services in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations. 2 1.2.7 Reports . Contractor shall prepare written reports in such form and substance as the Company requests. Contractor shall make themselves available for regular weekly team meetings. 1.2.8 Communications . Contractor shall report to the representative of the Company concerning each item of work assigned to Contractor by such Company representative. 1.3 Independent Contractor . This is not an agreement for employment, full time or otherwise. Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Agreement, Contractor shall act as and be deemed to be an independent contractor for all purposes of this Agreement and shall not act as or be deemed to be an employee of the Company. Contractor shall not hold Contractor out as a member, partner, or employee of the Company, and shall not enter into any contract or incur any liability in the Company's name without the Company's prior written approval. Subject to the instructions from the Company as to Contractor’s obligations for any specific contract work assignment, Contractor shall have responsibility for determining the appropriate means and methods to be used in performance of Contractor’s obligations under this Agreement. 1.3.1 Workmen's Compensation . The Company shall not be obligated to pay for or on behalf of Contractor workmen's compensation premium assessments; however, any such payment by Company (if any) shall not alter or affect the parties' relationship hereunder, and shall not constitute Contractor as a full time or regular employee of the Company, such workmen's compensation premiums to be paid solely for the convenience of the parties and in the exclusive discretion of the Company. 1.3.2 Taxes, Benefits, Etc. The Company shall have no liability for payment of or withholding of taxes of Contractor’s social security premiums, federal, state or city income taxes, retirement or other Company benefits or any other charges traditionally paid by the Company on behalf of its full-time employees. 1.4 Documents and Property . The data, drawings, maps, plans, reports or other information delivered to or prepared by Contractor and for which Contractor is compensated pursuant to this Agreement shall be the property of the Company. All such information which is the property of the Company under this Agreement shall be delivered to the Company by Contractor upon completion of Contractor's obligations under this Agreement, and shall not be reprinted, distributed, published or disclosed to any other party by Contractor, except as provided in this Agreement. 3 This Section shall not apply to data which Contractor independently possesses or prepares for a property or prospect before being engaged by the Company to provide services in respect of such property or prospect. All non-consumable materials or equipment purchased or leased by the Contractor under this Agreement for which Contractor is reimbursed by the Company shall become the property of the Company upon such reimbursement and shall be delivered to the Company upon completion of Contractor's obligations under this Agreement or otherwise disposed of at the Company's direction. 1.5 Insurance . Contractor shall procure and, at all times during the performance of this Agreement, maintain in full force and effect at Contractor's own expense the following insurance: 1.5.1 Unless waived by the Company, workmen's compensation insurance for Contractor as required by law. 1.5.2 Comprehensive general liability, personal injury liability and property damage liability, in an amount not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000.00) per occurrence. 1.5.3 Automobile, bodily injury and property damage liability insurance covering automobiles owned by Contractor and used in the performance of this Agreement in such amounts not less than Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($600,000.00) per occurrence, Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000.00) per person for bodily and One Hundred Thousand Dollars ($100,000.00) per occurrence for property damage. Whenever the Company reasonably requests, Contractor shall furnish to the Company evidence that such insurance is being maintained. 2. Term of Agreement . The term of this Agreement shall commence on September 21st, 2026 , notwithstanding that this Agreement is executed effective November 10, 2026 (the “Effective Date”), and the parties agree that this Agreement shall apply retroactively to, and govern, all services performed by Contractor for the Company from September 21st, 2026 through the Effective Date. Contractor may terminate this Agreement by delivering to the Company 60 days’ written notice. The Company may terminate this Agreement by delivering to Contractor 60 days’ written notice. 3. Contractor's Efforts; Time to be Devoted by Contractor . 3.1 Standard of Performance . Contractor shall cooperate with the Company and use maximum professional skill, diligence and care so that all work is scheduled and completed to the Company’s satisfaction. 3.2 Normal Hours . The parties acknowledge that Contractor's services under this Agreement shall be provided on a fifty percent (50%) time retainer basis. Contractor shall devote approximately fifty percent (50%) of their working time, estimated at twenty (20) hours per week or eighty (80) hours per month, to the Company. 4 The Contractor may determine the manner in which such hours are scheduled, provided that the Services are performed in a timely, professional, and responsive manner, and that all agreed deliverables, deadlines, and Company expectations are met. 4. Office Space . The Company expects the Contractor to provide a suitable working space within their home office. The Contractor may be based anywhere that allows them to fulfill their role and has high speed internet connection. The Company and Contractor acknowledge that, if additional local office space is needed or desired in the future, the Company will reimburse the Contractor for the reasonable cost of such office space, up to a maximum of $1,000 per month , subject to prior discussion and approval by the Company. As of the Effective Date of this Agreement, no such additional office space or reimbursement has been approved or is applicable. 5. Compensation . Monthly Retainer In consideration for the Services provided by the Contractor under this Agreement, the Company shall pay the Contractor a monthly retainer of Eight Thousand Three Hundred and Thirty Tree Dollars ($8,333.33) , equivalent to One Hundred Thousand Dollars ($100,000) per annum, based on a fifty percent (50%) time commitment. Contractor shall furnish the Company with narrative monthly statements including expenses incurred. The Company shall pay the compensation payable to Contractor within fifteen (15) days after Contractor's delivery of Contractor’s monthly billing. Equity Compensation As part of the Contractor’s compensation, the Company shall provide the Contractor with an equity award having an aggregate target value of approximately US$250,000, subject to the terms of the applicable equity incentive plan and award agreement. The equity award shall vest in three instalments as set out below, from the Contractors commencement date - 1. $50,000 on 6 months service and the Company achieving a $75m market capitalisation, 2. $100,000 on 12 months service and with completion of a first drilling exploration program that delivers an ore grade intercept, and 3. $100,000 on 24 months service and the Company delivering an initial Inferred Resource for an uplisting to a major exchange (NYSE or Nasdaq), These are also subject to the Contractor’s continued service through each applicable vesting date. 5 The Company and Contractor shall cooperate in good faith to structure the equity award in a manner intended to minimize adverse tax consequences to the Contractor, to the extent permitted under applicable law. The Company shall also grant the Contractor an option award, with the number of options, exercise price, vesting schedule, and other terms to be mutually agreed upon and documented in the applicable equity award agreement. The incentive equity and option award details will be completed by the Board with the Contractor following the completion of the Apex North transaction and successful re-listing on the OTC, and $3m initial capital raising immediately post OTC relisting. To qualify for any equity participation or bonus payment under this clause, the Contractor must be actively engaged by the Company: (a) when the Company and the third-party counterparty execute and deliver the transaction agreement or instrument; and (b) when the Company receives the consideration payable or deliverable in respect of the transaction. If the Contractor resigns or this Agreement is terminated, or is no longer actively engaged by the Company for any reason after the Company enters a transaction subject to this Section 5 and before the receipt of such consideration by the Company, the Contractor shall have no entitlement to and the Company shall not be obligated to pay or deliver to Contractor and interest in or share of any consideration or payment paid or delivered to the Company after which accrues after the Contractor’s resignation or termination of this Agreement. The Contractor acknowledges that the potential value of any equity instruments or bonus consideration issued pursuant to this clause may range from negligible to significant and will depend on factors including, but not limited to, exploration results, project outcomes, commodity prices, market conditions, liquidity, vesting terms, escrow restrictions, and the financial position of the issuer. The Company makes no representation or warranty as to the present or future value, liquidity, transferability, vesting, tax treatment, or ultimate realizable value of any such consideration paid or delivered to the Company. The Contractor acknowledges and agrees that all monetary and project participation compensation payable or deliverable to the Contractor under this Agreement are provided as consideration for services rendered in an independent contractor capacity. The Contractor shall be solely responsible for reporting and paying any and all federal, state, local, and other applicable taxes, including income tax, self-employment tax, capital gains tax, and any other tax obligations arising from or related to the receipt, holding, vesting, exercise, transfer, sale, or disposition of such equity instruments or bonus consideration. the Company shall have no obligation to withhold, remit, or pay any taxes on behalf of the Contractor, except to the extent required by applicable law. 6 6. Expenses . 6.1 Reimbursed Expenses . Subject to the provisions of Section 6.2, the Company shall reimburse Contractor for: 6.1.1 Reasonable travel expenses for pre-approved travel, including without limitation, lodging and food, and transportation during Contractor's engagement. 6.1.2 The Company agrees to pay Contractor a mileage reimbursement in accordance with the prevailing IRS standard mileage rate (currently $0.725 per mile) for all authorized field work-related travel, for which Contractor uses Contractor's own motor vehicle on behalf of the Company. Such motor vehicle to be owned, operated, insured and maintained solely by Contractor and solely at the expense of Contractor. Contractor shall maintain and deliver to the Company a log for the miles for which reimbursement is sought, including a description of the area traveled and the reasons for such travel. 6.1.3 Out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred for Contractor’s performance of the services to be performed under this Agreement. 6.1.4 Other expenses reasonably incurred under this Agreement, provided that such expenses have been made with the Company's prior approval and such expenses are submitted for reimbursement for pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. 6.2 Record Keeping . Contractor shall keep an accurate account of all expenses necessarily incurred by Contractor and will deliver a monthly detailed statement of Contractor’s expenses incurred. Contractor shall submit to the Company copies of the original scanned receipts, vouchers and invoices representing such expenses. The Company will pay such expenses within the time for payment of Contractor's compensation under this Agreement. 7. Assignment and Delegation . Except as specifically provided to the contrary, Contractor may not assign any of Contractor's rights or interests or delegate Contractor's obligations or duties under this Agreement except upon the Company's prior written consent. Contractor acknowledges that the Company may acquire or become an affiliate of one or more other corporations and that Contractor agrees that the Company may assign its rights under this Agreement to such other companies. Contractor agrees to perform Contractor’s obligations under this Agreement for such other companies. 7 8. Confidential Data . 8.1 Property of Company . Contractor acknowledges and agrees that the data, information, reports, surveys and other documents provided to Contractor by the Company, created or developed by the Company, created or developed by Contractor during Contractor’s performance of Contractor’s obligations under this Agreement or acquired by the Company or Contractor in the performance of their obligations under this Agreement shall be held in strictest confidence. This Section shall not apply to data which Contractor independently possessed or prepared for a property or prospect before being engaged by the Company to work on such property or prospect. Contractor shall retain the right to use the data which Contractor previously possessed or prepared. Contractor acknowledges and agrees that any data or other information prepared by Contractor for the work performed pursuant to this Agreement and for which Contractor is compensated under this Agreement shall at all times belong to the Company and shall be usable now or in the future by the Company for any purposes without payment or charge, except the payments which the Company is obligated to pay to Contractor under this Agreement. 8.2 Nondisclosure by Contractor . Contractor shall not disclose to any third party any confidential data or information communicated to it or to its employees or agents by the Company and shall not use, or allow the use of, any of such data or information for the benefit of any other person, the Company or corporation without the Company's prior written consent. Contractor acknowledges that the Company’s clients are or may become companies or wholly-owned subsidiaries of companies whose shares are listed on a securities exchange for trading by the public. Contractor agrees and covenants to comply with applicable securities laws and regulations regarding nondisclosure of the Company’s and clients’ data and information. 8.3 Access to Company Financial Information and Funds. The Contractor may, in the course of providing the Services, be granted access to the Company’s bank account information, tax filings, financial records, accounting systems, passwords, login credentials, payment platforms, and other confidential financial information. The Contractor shall use such access solely for authorized Company business and only in accordance with the Company’s instructions and approval procedures. The Contractor shall not withdraw, transfer, spend, redirect, misappropriate, or otherwise use any Company funds, assets, accounts, or financial information for any unauthorized purpose. The Contractor shall be personally liable to the Company for any unauthorized withdrawal, transfer, payment, expenditure, misappropriation, misuse, fraud, or other unauthorized use of Company funds, accounts, credentials, or financial information, including any losses, costs, fees, penalties, damages, and reasonable legal expenses incurred by the Company as a result of such conduct. The Contractor shall maintain the confidentiality and security of all Company passwords, login credentials, banking information, and financial records, and shall not disclose, share, store insecurely, or permit access to such information by any unauthorized person. The Contractor shall immediately notify the Company of any suspected or actual unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, misuse, or compromise of Company financial information or credentials. 8 The Contractor’s obligations under this Section 8.3 shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement. 8.4 Term . Contractor's obligations under this Section 8 shall exist during the term of this Agreement, any renewals or extensions and after the termination of this Agreement. 9. Contracting for Others . 9.1 Consulting Permitted . The Contractor is free to engage in other employment or contract work during the term of this Agreement, provided that such activities do not create a conflict of interest, interfere with the performance of the Contractor’s duties under this Agreement, or involve the use or disclosure of the Company’s confidential or proprietary information. The Contractor agrees to promptly disclose to the Company any potential conflict of interest that may arise in connection with other work or business activities, in particularly in relation to project generation and exploration activities. 10. Indemnity . Each party shall indemnify and save harmless the other from and against any and all claims, demands, awards, actions and proceedings by whomsoever made, brought or prosecuted, loss, damage or expense suffered or incurred by the party, including attorneys' fees, which are based upon contract or tort, and arise from or are in any way connected with the performance by the parties of their respective obligations under this Agreement or anything done or maintained by the parties as required under this Agreement, except and to the extent the same was negligently caused by the party seeking indemnification. 11. Notices and Payments . 11.1 Notices . Any notices required or authorized to be given by this Agreement shall be in written form. Any notices required or authorized to be given by this Agreement may be sent by email, commercial courier, registered or certified delivery, postage prepaid and return receipt requested, addressed to the proper party at the following address or such address as the party shall have designated to the other parties in accordance with this Section. 9 Any notice required or authorized to be delivered by this Agreement shall be deemed to have been sufficiently delivered or served in written form if: (a) mailed in accordance with this Section; (b) personally delivered to the proper party; or (c) delivered by email or other electronic transmission and actually received by such party. Delivery of notice shall be effective on the first business day after the party deposits the notice for mailing or delivers the notice by the other means authorized in this Section, as applicable. If to Company: Brett Mitchell: *** If to Contractor: Lyndsey Wright: *** Payments . Any payment to be made to Contractor shall be deemed properly made if a check or electronic transfer payable to Contractor in the appropriate amount is delivered to Contractor in accordance with the provisions of this Section. Any such payment shall be deemed to be received by Contractor pursuant to this Section provided such check or electronic transfer is honored on presentment. All dollar amounts described in this Agreement are United States dollars. 12. Miscellaneous . 12.1 Company Holiday Period & Leave. The Company observes an annual shutdown period from December 24 through January 3 each year. During this period, the Contractor shall continue to receive their normal monthly retainer, but shall not be expected to perform Services, respond to routine Company matters, or otherwise be available for work, unless otherwise agreed in advance or required in the case of an urgent matter. The annual shutdown period shall not reduce the Contractor’s monthly retainer or otherwise affect the Contractor’s standing under this Agreement. 12.2 Successors . This Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the Company, its successors and assigns, and Contractor, Contractor's heirs, executors, successors and permitted assigns. 12.3 Entire Agreement . The parties agree that the whole agreement between them is written in this Agreement and this Agreement shall constitute the entire contract between the parties. There are no terms or conditions, express or implied, other than stated in this Agreement. This Agreement may be amended or modified only by an instrument in writing, signed by the parties with the same formality as this Agreement. 10 12.4 Governing Law and Forum Selection . This Agreement shall be construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of Nevada, and any litigation concerning this Agreement shall be commenced in Washoe County, State of Nevada. The forum for any action regarding the construction or enforcement of this Agreement shall be the Second Judicial District Court, Washoe County, Reno, Nevada. Each party consents and submits to the jurisdiction of the Second Judicial District Court. 12.5 Severability . If any part, term or provision of this Agreement is held by the courts to be illegal or in conflict with any law of the United States or any state, the validity of the remaining portions or provision shall not be affected and the rights and obligations of the parties shall be construed and enforced as if the Agreement did not contain the particular part, term or provision held to be invalid. 12.6 Headings . Headings used herein are for convenience of reference only. 12.7 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed simultaneously in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument. The parties have executed this Agreement effective November 10, 2026. INTEGRAL TECHNOLOGIES, INC. By Brett Mitchell, CEO CONTRACTOR By Lyndsey Wright 11

text: EX-10.4 8 ex_1026579.htm EXHIBIT 10.4 ex_1026579.htm Exhibit 10.4 THE EXCHANGE CONTEMPLATED HEREIN IS INTENDED TO COMPORT WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 3(a)(9) OF THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933. EXCHANGE AGREEMENT This Exchange Agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is entered into as of November 10, 2026 by and among (i) SBI Investments LLC, 2014-1, a Delaware limited liability company (“ SBI ”), (ii) C/M Capital Master Fund, LP, a Delaware limited Partnership (“ CM ”), (iii) WVP Emerging Manager Onshore Fund, LLC – C/M Capital Series, a Delaware limited liability company (“ WVP ” and, together with SBI and CM, each a “ Recipient ” and collectively, the “ Recipients ”), and (iv) Integral Technologies, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Company ”). A. The Company previously issued to each Recipient notes as described on Exhibit A (the “ Prior Securities ”). B. Each Recipient and the Company desire to exchange (such exchanges, collectively, the “ Exchange ”) the Prior Securities for shares of Series D Preferred Stock, with the rights, preferences, privileges and restrictions set forth in the Certificate of Designation attached as Exhibit B (the “ New Securities ”), on the terms and conditions of this Agreement, with the number of shares issuable to each Recipient to be set forth on a schedule delivered at Closing. C. The Exchange will consist of each Recipient cancelling its Prior Securities in exchange for its allocable portion of the New Securities. D. Other than the surrender of the Prior Securities, no consideration of any kind whatsoever shall be given by any Recipient to the Company in connection with this Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: 1. Recitals and Definitions . Each of the parties hereto acknowledges and agrees that the recitals set forth above in this Agreement are true and accurate, are contractual in nature, and are hereby incorporated into and made a part of this Agreement. For purposes of this Agreement, “ Transaction Documents ” means the Prior Securities and each other agreement, certificate, instrument or document executed or delivered in connection with the issuance or ownership of the Prior Securities. 2. Terms of the Exchange . At the Closing (as defined below), (i) each Recipient shall surrender its Prior Securities to the Company for cancellation, (ii) all obligations of the Company under the Prior Securities shall be deemed satisfied and discharged in full upon such cancellation, and (iii) the Company shall issue and deliver to each Recipient its allocable portion of the New Securities, free and clear of all liens, claims, pledges, security interests and other encumbrances, with no consideration payable by any Recipient other than the surrender of its Prior Securities. 3. Closing . The closing of the transactions contemplated hereby (the “ Closing ”), including the surrender of the Prior Securities and the issuance and delivery of the New Securities to each Recipient, shall occur on the date mutually agreed to by the Company and the Recipients by the remote exchange of executed PDF documents and any other closing deliverables required by this Agreement. 1 4. Holding Period and Tacking . The Company represents, warrants and agrees that, for purposes of Rule 144 (“ Rule 144 ”) under the Securities Act of 1933 (the “ Securities Act ”), the New Securities are being issued by the same issuer that issued the Prior Securities and the holding period of the New Securities will include the holding period of the Prior Securities exchanged for the New Securities. The Company and each Recipient hereby represent that (i) the transactions contemplated hereby and all other documents associated with this transaction are intended to comply with the requirements of Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities Act, (ii) no commission or other remuneration has been or will be paid or given, directly or indirectly, for soliciting the Exchange, and (iii) no Recipient currently is or will be upon the Closing (individually or together as a group) deemed an “affiliate” as defined in Rule 144. The Company shall, at its sole cost and upon any Recipient’s reasonable request, provide or cause its counsel to provide any legal opinion, transfer agent instructions and other documentation reasonably necessary to evidence the foregoing and to permit Rule 144 tacking or removal of restrictive legends when available under applicable law. The Company acknowledges and understands that the representations and agreements of the Company in this Section 4 are a material inducement to each Recipient’s decision to consummate the transactions contemplated herein. The Company agrees not to take a position contrary to this Section 4 in any document, statement, setting, or situation . 5. The Company’s Representations, Warranties and Agreements . In order to induce each Recipient to enter into this Agreement, the Company, for itself, and for its affiliates, successors and assigns, hereby acknowledges, represents, warrants and agrees as follows: (a) the Company has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to incur and perform all obligations and covenants contained herein, all of which have been duly authorized by all proper and necessary corporate action, (b) no consent, approval, filing or registration with or notice to any governmental authority is required as a condition to the validity of this Agreement or the performance of any of the obligations of the Company hereunder, (c) the issuance of the New Securities is duly authorized by all necessary corporate action and the New Securities are validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable, free and clear of all taxes, liens, claims, pledges, mortgages, restrictions, obligations, security interests and encumbrances of any kind, nature and description, (d) the Company has not received any consideration in any form whatsoever for entering into this Agreement, other than the surrender of the Prior Securities, and (e) the Company has taken no action which would give rise to any claim by any person for a brokerage commission, placement agent or finder’s fee or other similar payment by the Company related to this Agreement. 6. Recipients’ Representations, Warranties and Agreements . In order to induce the Company to enter into this Agreement, each Recipient, severally and not jointly, for itself, and for its affiliates, successors and assigns, hereby acknowledges, represents, warrants and agrees as follows: (a) such Recipient has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to incur and perform all obligations and covenants contained herein, all of which have been duly authorized by all proper and necessary action, (b) this Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by such Recipient and constitutes the legal, valid and binding obligation of such Recipient, enforceable against such Recipient in accordance with its terms, (c) no consent, approval, filing or registration with or notice to any governmental authority is required as a condition to the validity of this Agreement or the performance of any of the obligations of such Recipient hereunder, (d) such Recipient has taken no action which would give rise to any claim by any person for a brokerage commission, placement agent or finder’s fee or other similar payment by such Recipient or the Company related to this Agreement, (e) such Recipient is the sole legal and beneficial owner of its Prior Securities, free and clear of all liens, claims and encumbrances, and (f) such Recipient is acquiring its New Securities for investment purposes and not with a present view to any distribution in violation of the Securities Act. 7. Governing Law; Venue; Jury Waiver . This Agreement and the New Securities shall be construed and enforced in accordance with, and all questions concerning the construction, validity, interpretation and performance of this Agreement shall be governed by, the internal laws of the State of Nevada, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflict of law provision or rule that would cause the application of the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Nevada. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Nevada for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby, and each party irrevocably waives any objection to venue in such courts, including any objection based on forum non conveniens. THE COMPANY AND EACH RECIPIENT HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO, AND AGREES NOT TO REQUEST, A JURY TRIAL FOR THE ADJUDICATION OF ANY DISPUTE HEREUNDER OR IN CONNECTION WITH OR ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY TRANSACTION CONTEMPLATED HEREBY. 2 8. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts with the same effect as if all signing parties had signed the same document. All counterparts shall be construed together and constitute the same instrument. The exchange of copies of this Agreement and of signature pages by facsimile transmission or other electronic transmission (including email) shall constitute effective execution and delivery of this Agreement as to the parties and may be used in lieu of the original Agreement for all purposes. Signatures of the parties transmitted by facsimile transmission or other electronic transmission (including DocuSign) shall be deemed to be their original signatures for all purposes. 9. Attorneys’ Fees . In the event of any arbitration or action at law or in equity to enforce or interpret the terms of this Agreement, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover from the non-prevailing party its reasonable attorneys’ fees, costs and expenses incurred in connection with such arbitration, litigation and/or dispute, including any fees, costs and expenses incurred on appeal or in enforcing any judgment or award. The prevailing party shall be determined by the arbitrator or court based on the party that substantially prevailed on the merits of the dispute. Nothing herein shall restrict or impair an arbitrator’s or a court’s power to award fees and expenses for frivolous or bad faith pleading. 10. No Reliance . Each party acknowledges and agrees that the other party has not made any representations or warranties except as expressly set forth in this Agreement and, in making its decision to enter into the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, is not relying on any representation, warranty, covenant or promise of the other party or its officers, directors, members, managers, equity holders, agents or representatives other than as expressly set forth in this Agreement; provided, however, that nothing in this Agreement shall limit or preclude any claim based on fraud, intentional misrepresentation or willful misconduct. 11. Entire Agreement . This Agreement, together with the exhibits hereto and the Prior Securities, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings and communications, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter. 12. Severability . If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified to achieve the objective of the parties to the fullest extent permitted by law, and the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect. 13. Amendments . This Agreement may be amended, modified, or supplemented only by written agreement of the parties. No provision of this Agreement may be waived except in writing signed by the party against whom such waiver is sought to be enforced. 14. Successors and Assigns . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns. This Agreement or any of the severable rights and obligations inuring to the benefit of or to be performed by any Recipient hereunder may be assigned by such Recipient to a third party, including its financing sources, in whole or in part. The Company may not assign this Agreement or any of its obligations herein without the prior written consent of each Recipient, and any attempted assignment in violation of this Section shall be null and void. 3 15. Continuing Enforceability . Except as otherwise modified by this Agreement, the Prior Securities and each of the other Transaction Documents shall remain in full force and effect, enforceable in accordance with all of their original terms and provisions until the Closing. Upon the Closing, the Prior Securities shall be cancelled and discharged as provided in this Agreement. If the Closing does not occur, nothing in this Agreement shall impair any Recipient’s rights under its Prior Securities or any other Transaction Document. This Agreement shall not be effective or binding unless and until it is fully executed and delivered by each Recipient and the Company. 16. Time of Essence . Time is of the essence with respect to each and every provision of this Agreement. 17. Notices . Any notice or communication permitted or required hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed sufficiently given (a) when delivered by hand, (b) on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, (c) on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, or (d) when sent by email, if sent during the recipient’s normal business hours and the sender does not receive an automated bounceback or other notice of non-delivery, and otherwise on the next business day, in each case to the addresses and email addresses set forth on the signature page below or to such other address or email address as either party may designate by notice in accordance with this Section. 18. Further Assurances . Each party shall do and perform or cause to be done and performed, all such further acts and things, and shall execute and deliver all such other agreements, certificates, instruments and documents, as the other party may reasonably request in order to carry out the intent and accomplish the purposes of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. [Remainder of page intentionally left blank] 4 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned have executed this Agreement as of the date first set forth above. text: EX-10.5 9 ex_1023883.htm EXHIBIT 10.5 ex_1023883.htm Exhibit 10.5 PROMISSORY NOTE ACCEPTANCE AGREEMENT THIS PROMISSORY NOTE ACCEPTANCE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of November 10, 2026 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Integral Technologies, Inc. , a Nevada corporation (the “Issuer”), and [__________], an individual (the “Recipient”). RECITALS WHEREAS , the Recipient has previously rendered services to the Issuer in connection with the Issuer’s business operations (the “Services”); WHEREAS , as of the Effective Date, the Issuer owes to the Recipient certain compensation for the Services in the amount of $_______ (the “Compensation Owed”); WHEREAS , the Issuer desires to issue to the Recipient, and the Recipient desires to accept, a promissory note (the “Note”) in the principal amount of U.S. $300,000 (the “Principal Amount”), which Principal Amount is less than the Compensation Owed, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A , as a negotiated compromise and in full satisfaction and discharge of the Compensation Owed to the Recipient; and WHEREAS , each party desires to release the other party from certain claims as set forth herein. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the mutual covenants, agreements, representations, and warranties set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: ARTICLE I — ISSUANCE AND ACCEPTANCE OF PROMISSORY NOTE Section 1.1 Issuance of Note. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, at the Closing (as defined below), the Issuer shall execute and deliver to the Recipient a Note in the Principal Amount, in full satisfaction and discharge of the Compensation Owed to the Recipient. The Note shall be substantially in the form of Exhibit A attached hereto. Section 1.2 Satisfaction of Compensation. The Recipient acknowledges and agrees that the Principal Amount is less than the Compensation Owed and that the Recipient’s receipt and acceptance of the Note constitutes a negotiated compromise and full satisfaction and discharge of all Compensation Owed to the Recipient by the Issuer for the Services, including any portion of the Compensation Owed in excess of the Principal Amount. Except for the Issuer’s obligations under this Agreement and the Note, the Recipient shall have no further claims against the Issuer or any Issuer Released Party with respect to the Compensation Owed, the Services, or any prior employment, consulting, or service relationship between the Recipient and the Issuer. Section 1.3 Payment Terms. Principal, accrued interest, and all other amounts payable under the Note shall be due and payable when and as set forth in the Note. Payments shall be made in lawful money of the United States by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by the Recipient, or by such other method as the Issuer and the Recipient may agree in writing. Section 1.4 Closing. The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the “Closing”) shall take place on the Effective Date, or at such other time and place as the parties may mutually agree in writing. At the Closing, the Issuer shall deliver to the Recipient the Issuer’s duly executed Note. ARTICLE II — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE ISSUER The Issuer hereby represents and warrants to the Recipient as of the Effective Date as follows: Section 2.1 Organization and Good Standing. The Issuer is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Nevada. The Issuer has all requisite corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and to carry on its business as presently conducted. Section 2.2 Authorization; Enforceability. The Issuer has full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of the Issuer. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by the Issuer and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Issuer, enforceable against the Issuer in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, or similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and by general principles of equity (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in a proceeding at law or in equity). Section 2.3 Valid Obligation. The Note, when executed and delivered by the Issuer in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, will constitute a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Issuer, enforceable against the Issuer in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, or similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and by general principles of equity (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in a proceeding at law or in equity). Section 2.4 No Conflicts. The execution, delivery, and performance by the Issuer of this Agreement, and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby, do not and will not (a) violate or conflict with the Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws of the Issuer, (b) violate or conflict with any law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree applicable to the Issuer, or (c) result in a breach of, constitute a default under, or require any consent, notice, approval, or waiver under any material agreement or instrument to which the Issuer is a party or by which the Issuer is bound, except for any consent, notice, approval, or waiver that has been obtained or given prior to the Closing. ARTICLE III — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE RECIPIENT The Recipient hereby represents and warrants to the Issuer as of the Effective Date as follows: Section 3.1 Authority; Enforceability. The Recipient has full legal capacity and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by the Recipient and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Recipient, enforceable against the Recipient in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, or similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and by general principles of equity (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in a proceeding at law or in equity). Section 3.2 Receipt of Information. The Recipient has been given access to such information regarding the Issuer and its business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects as the Recipient has deemed necessary or appropriate to make an informed decision with respect to the acceptance of the Note. The Recipient has had the opportunity to ask questions of, and receive answers from, representatives of the Issuer concerning the Issuer and the terms and conditions of the Note. Section 3.3 No Reliance. The Recipient acknowledges that the Recipient has made his or her own independent investigation and evaluation of the Issuer and its ability to perform its obligations under the Note. The Recipient is not relying on any representation, warranty, or statement of the Issuer or any of its agents, representatives, or attorneys other than those expressly set forth in this Agreement. The Recipient is relying solely on such advisors and not on any statements or representations of the Issuer or any of its agents with respect to such tax consequences. The Recipient shall not sell, assign, pledge, transfer, or otherwise dispose of the Note except in compliance with applicable securities laws and the terms of the Note.
