The Recipient has such knowledge and experience in financial and business matters as to be capable of evaluating the merits and risks of accepting the Note, has independently evaluated the risks of accepting the Note in lieu of cash payment, and is able to bear the economic risk of accepting the Note, including the risk that the Note may not be repaid in full or on time. ARTICLE IV — MUTUAL GENERAL RELEASE Section 4.1 Release by Issuer. Effective as of the Closing, the Issuer, on behalf of itself and its successors, assigns, parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, attorneys, heirs, and executors (collectively, the “Issuer Releasing Parties”), hereby fully, finally, and forever releases, acquits, and discharges the Recipient and the Recipient’s heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the “Recipient Released Parties”) from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, accounts, bonds, covenants, contracts, agreements, judgments, charges, complaints, promises, damages, costs, losses, obligations, liabilities, and expenses of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, fixed or contingent, liquidated or unliquidated, matured or unmatured, at law or in equity (collectively, “Claims”), that the Issuer Releasing Parties ever had, now have, or may hereafter have against the Recipient Released Parties arising out of, relating to, or in connection with the Services rendered by the Recipient to the Issuer prior to the Effective Date. Section 4.2 Release by Recipient. Effective as of the Closing, the Recipient, on behalf of himself or herself and his or her heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the “Recipient Releasing Parties”), hereby fully, finally, and forever releases, acquits, and discharges the Issuer and its predecessors, successors, assigns, parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, and each of their respective past, present, and future officers, directors, managers, employees, stockholders, members, partners, agents, representatives, attorneys, insurers, heirs, executors, administrators, employee benefit plans, and fiduciaries (collectively, the “Issuer Released Parties”) from any and all Claims that the Recipient Releasing Parties ever had, now have, or may hereafter have against the Issuer Released Parties arising out of, relating to, or in connection with (a) the Compensation Owed, including any portion of the Compensation Owed in excess of the Principal Amount and any wages, salary, bonuses, commissions, equity, incentive compensation, benefits, expense reimbursements, penalties, interest, attorneys’ fees, or other amounts allegedly arising from the Services or any employment, consulting, or service relationship between the Recipient and the Issuer, (b) the Services rendered by the Recipient to the Issuer, (c) any employment, consulting, or service relationship between the Recipient and the Issuer, (d) any prior dealings between the Recipient and the Issuer, and (e) any facts, acts, omissions, events, or circumstances occurring on or before the Effective Date relating to the foregoing. Section 4.3 Waiver of Unknown Claims. Each party acknowledges that such party may hereafter discover Claims or facts in addition to or different from those that such party now knows or believes to exist with respect to the subject matter of the releases contained in this Article IV. Nevertheless, it is the intention of each party to fully, finally, and forever settle and release all Claims that exist, may exist, or heretofore have existed as set forth in Sections 4.1 and 4.2. In furtherance of such intention, each party hereby expressly waives and relinquishes, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any and all rights or benefits that such party may have under any statute, rule, or principle of common law that would otherwise limit the effect of the releases contained herein to those Claims actually known or suspected to exist at the time of execution of this Agreement. Each party acknowledges that such party is familiar with Section 1542 of the Civil Code of the State of California, which provides as follows: “A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party. ” Each party, being aware of said code section, hereby expressly waives any rights such party may have thereunder, as well as any rights under any other statute, rule, or principle of common law of similar effect in the State of Nevada or any other jurisdiction. Section 4.4 Knowing and Voluntary Waiver. Each party acknowledges and agrees that (a) such party has carefully read and fully understands all of the provisions of this Article IV, (b) such party is voluntarily entering into this Agreement and the releases contained herein, (c) such party has had the opportunity to consult with legal counsel of such party’s own choosing prior to executing this Agreement, (d) such party has not relied upon any representation or statement made by any other party or any other party’s agents, representatives, or attorneys with regard to the subject matter, basis, or effect of this Agreement, and (e) such party understands and acknowledges the significance and consequences of the releases contained herein. Section 4.5 Exceptions to Release. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the releases set forth in this Article IV shall not apply to (a) any Claims arising out of or relating to any breach of this Agreement or the Note occurring after the Effective Date, (b) any rights of any party to enforce the terms and conditions of this Agreement or the Note, (c) any Claims that cannot be waived or released as a matter of law, including any right to file a charge or complaint with, communicate with, or participate in any investigation or proceeding conducted by any governmental agency, or (d) any Claims arising after the Effective Date that are based on acts or omissions first occurring after the Effective Date. Section 4.6 No Admission of Liability. Neither this Agreement nor the issuance of the Note shall be construed as an admission by any party of any liability, wrongdoing, or violation of law, all of which are expressly denied. ARTICLE V — TAX MATTERS Section 5.1 Tax Treatment; Responsibility. The Recipient acknowledges that the Issuer has made no representations regarding the tax treatment of the issuance of the Note, the discharge of any portion of the Compensation Owed, or the receipt of payments under the Note, and that the Recipient is not relying on the Issuer for any tax advice. The Recipient shall be solely responsible for all taxes, penalties, and interest imposed on or with respect to the Recipient arising from the transactions contemplated by this Agreement or payments under the Note. The Recipient agrees, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, to indemnify and hold harmless the Issuer Released Parties from any liability for such taxes, penalties, or interest, except to the extent attributable to the Issuer’s failure to withhold, remit, or report amounts that the Issuer actually withheld or was legally required to withhold. Any amounts so withheld shall be treated as having been paid to the Recipient for all purposes of this Agreement. ARTICLE VI — MISCELLANEOUS Section 6.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Nevada, without regard to any choice of law or conflict of law rules or provisions that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. Section 6.2 Entire Agreement; Order of Precedence. This Agreement, including Exhibit A attached hereto, and the Note issued hereunder constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersede all prior agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, between the parties with respect thereto. There are no representations, warranties, covenants, or other agreements between the parties relating to the subject matter hereof other than those expressly set forth or referred to herein. In the event of any direct conflict between this Agreement and the Note, (a) this Agreement shall control with respect to the issuance and acceptance of the Note, the satisfaction and release of the Compensation Owed, and the releases set forth herein, and (b) the Note shall control with respect to payment, prepayment, interest, maturity, default, remedies, collection costs, and enforcement of the indebtedness evidenced thereby. Section 6.3 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect under any applicable law or rule in any jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Agreement or any other jurisdiction, and this Agreement shall be reformed, construed, and enforced in such jurisdiction as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision had never been contained herein. Section 6.4 Amendment and Waiver. This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by the Issuer and the Recipient. The Note may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by the Issuer and the Recipient. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement or the Note shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by the party to be bound thereby. No waiver by any party of any breach or default hereunder shall be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach or default. Section 6.5 Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. The exchange of copies of this Agreement and signature pages by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by any other electronic means intended to preserve the original graphic and pictorial appearance of a document shall have the same effect as delivery of an original executed copy of this Agreement. The parties agree that this Agreement may be executed by electronic signature (including DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or similar technology), and that any such electronic signature shall be deemed an original signature for all purposes and shall have the same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as a manually executed signature. Section 6.6 Successors and Assigns. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and permitted assigns. The Recipient may not assign this Agreement, the Note, or any rights or obligations hereunder or thereunder without the prior written consent of the Issuer, except by operation of law upon death or incapacity and subject in all cases to applicable securities laws and the terms of the Note. The Issuer may assign its rights and obligations hereunder or under the Note to any successor entity in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization, conversion, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, provided that such successor assumes the Issuer’s payment obligations under the Note. Any notice or communication permitted or required hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed sufficiently given (a) when delivered by hand, (b) on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, (c) on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, or (d) when sent by email, if sent during the recipient’s normal business hours and the sender does not receive an automated bounceback or other notice of non-delivery, and otherwise on the next business day, in each case to the addresses and email addresses set forth on the signature page below or to such other address or email address as either party may designate by notice in accordance with this Section. Section 6.8 Further Assurances. Each party shall execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, and agreements and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary or appropriate to effectuate the purposes of this Agreement. Section 6.9 No Third-Party Beneficiaries. Except as expressly set forth in Article IV with respect to the Released Parties, this Agreement is not intended to, and shall not, confer any rights or remedies upon any person other than the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Section 6.10 Construction. The parties have participated jointly in the negotiation and drafting of this Agreement, and in the event an ambiguity or question of intent or interpretation arises, this Agreement shall be construed as if drafted jointly by the parties, and no presumption or burden of proof shall arise favoring or disfavoring any party by virtue of the authorship of any of the provisions of this Agreement. The headings in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not limit or otherwise affect the meaning hereof. Section 6.11 Jurisdiction; Venue. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Nevada for any action, suit, or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the Note, and each party irrevocably waives any objection to venue or any claim that such courts are an inconvenient forum. This Note is issued pursuant to and in connection with that certain Promissory Note Acceptance Agreement, dated as of the date hereof, by and between Maker and Lender (the “ Acceptance Agreement ”). Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of any Event of Default, and notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Note, the outstanding principal balance of this Note and, to the extent permitted by applicable law, all accrued and unpaid interest, shall bear interest at a default rate per annum equal to the lesser of (i) 13% (i.e., the rate otherwise applicable under this Note plus an additional 5% per annum) and (ii) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, in each case accruing from the date such Event of Default occurs until such Event of Default is cured or waived or such amounts are paid in full. Such default interest shall be payable on demand and is in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other rights and remedies available to Lender under this Note. Interest (computed on the basis of a 360-day year for the actual number of days elapsed) on the outstanding balance of principal evidenced by this Promissory Note (this “ Note ”) shall accrue at a rate per annum equal to 8% from the Issuance Date until paid in full. Accrued interest shall be due and payable in arrears on the last day of each calendar quarter (each, an “ Interest Payment Date ”), commencing on the first such date occurring after the Issuance Date; provided that if any Interest Payment Date falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday in Nevada, such payment shall be due on the next business day. Any interest remaining unpaid on the Maturity Date shall be due and payable on the Maturity Date. On the date that is 18 months after the Issuance Date of this Note (the “ Maturity Date ”), all outstanding principal, any accrued and unpaid interest, and all other amounts due and payable hereunder shall be due and payable in full. Except as otherwise provided herein with respect to Interest Payment Dates, if any payment date under this Note falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday in Nevada, the payment shall be due on the next business day, and interest shall continue to accrue through such next business day. Each of the following shall constitute an event of default under this Note (each, an “ Event of Default ”): (i) Maker fails to make any payment of principal, interest (including any quarterly interest payment) or any other amount under this Note when due, and such failure continues for 10 business days after written notice from Lender; (ii) Maker breaches any material covenant or other obligation under this Note or the Acceptance Agreement, and such breach (if curable) is not cured within 30 days after written notice from Lender; (iii) any representation or warranty made by Maker in the Acceptance Agreement proves to have been materially false or misleading when made, and such breach (if curable) is not cured within 30 days after written notice from Lender; (iv) Maker commences a voluntary case or proceeding under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, receivership or similar law, consents to the entry of an order for relief in an involuntary case, consents to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian for Maker or for all or substantially all of Maker’s assets, or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors; (v) a court of competent jurisdiction enters an order or decree under any applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, receivership or similar law that (A) is for relief against Maker in an involuntary case, (B) appoints a receiver, trustee or custodian for Maker or for all or substantially all of Maker’s assets, or (C) orders the liquidation of Maker, and such order or decree remains unstayed, undismissed and in effect for 60 consecutive days; or (vi) Maker dissolves or ceases to conduct business operations. At any time after the occurrence and during the continuance of any Event of Default, Lender may, by written notice to Maker, declare the indebtedness evidenced by this Note, any note(s) or other obligation(s) taken in renewal, extension, substitution or modification of all or any part of such indebtedness, and all other obligations of Maker to Lender under this Note to be immediately due and payable without further demand upon or notice to Maker, and Lender shall be entitled to exercise all remedies provided by law and/or equity; provided that, upon the occurrence of an Event of Default described in clause (iv) or clause (v) of the preceding paragraph, all such amounts shall automatically become immediately due and payable without any action by Lender. Maker hereby waives presentment for payment, demand, notice of dishonor and protest and agrees that (i) Lender may release any indorser, surety, guarantor or other person liable on or with respect to this Note, in each case without notice to or further reservation of rights against Maker, any indorser, surety or guarantor and without in any way affecting or releasing the liability of Maker, any indorser, surety or guarantor, (ii) none of the terms or provisions hereof may be altered, modified or amended except pursuant to a written instrument signed by Maker and Lender, and (iii) no waiver of any term or provision hereof shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by the party to be bound thereby. No failure or delay by Lender in exercising any right, power or remedy under this Note shall operate as a waiver thereof, and no single or partial exercise of any such right, power or remedy shall preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power or remedy. Maker hereby agrees to pay all reasonable and documented out‑of‑pocket costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, incurred by Lender after an Event of Default in collecting the indebtedness evidenced by this Note or enforcing any of the rights, powers, remedies, and privileges of Lender hereunder. As used in this Note, the term “attorneys’ fees” means reasonable actual out-of-pocket charges and expenses for legal services rendered to or on behalf of Lender in connection with the collection of the indebtedness evidenced by this Note, whether incurred before the commencement of judicial proceedings or at trial, on appeal, or in prejudgment, postjudgment or bankruptcy proceedings. In no event shall the rate of interest charged under this Note exceed the maximum rate that may legally be charged to Maker for obligations of this nature under the laws of the State of Nevada. Any interest paid in excess of the legal limit shall be refunded to Maker or applied to the principal obligation under this Note, in each case to the extent required by applicable law. Each party hereto irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Nevada and agrees that any action, litigation or proceeding relating to this Note shall be brought exclusively in such courts. Each party hereto irrevocably waives any objection to venue in such courts and any claim that such courts are an inconvenient forum. Each party hereto agrees that a final judgment in any such action, litigation or proceeding shall be conclusive and may be enforced in other jurisdictions by suit on the judgment or in any other manner provided by law. Notices. All notices, requests, demands and other communications under this Note shall be in writing and shall be given in accordance with the notice provisions of the Acceptance Agreement, addressed to the parties at their respective addresses set forth on the signature page of the Acceptance Agreement (or such other address or email address as either party may designate by notice given in accordance with such provisions), and shall be deemed sufficiently given (a) when delivered by hand, (b) on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, (c) on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier, or (d) when sent by email, if sent during the recipient's normal business hours and the sender does not receive an automated bounceback or other notice of non-delivery, and otherwise on the next business day. To the extent that Lender receives any payment on account of any of Maker’s obligations and any such payment or any part thereof is subsequently invalidated, declared to be fraudulent or preferential, set aside, subordinated and/or required to be repaid to a trustee, receiver or any other person or entity under any bankruptcy act, state or federal law, common law or equitable cause, then, to the extent of such payment received, Maker’s obligations or part thereof intended to be satisfied shall be revived and continue in full force and effect as if such payment had not been received by Lender and applied on account of Maker’s obligations. Maker agrees that this Note shall be deemed to have been made under and shall be governed by the laws of the State of Nevada in all respects, including matters of construction, validity and performance, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law rule that would cause the laws of any other jurisdiction to apply. If any provision of this Note shall be deemed unenforceable under applicable law, such provision shall be ineffective, but only to the extent of such unenforceability, without invalidating the remainder of such provision or the remaining provisions of this Note. All of the terms and provisions of this Note shall be applicable to and be binding upon Maker and each indorser, surety, guarantor and other person who is or may become liable for payment hereof, and their respective heirs, personal representatives, successors and permitted assigns, and shall inure to the benefit of Lender and its successors and permitted assigns. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any sale, assignment, pledge, transfer or other disposition of this Note or any rights hereunder by Lender shall be subject to the transfer restrictions set forth in the Acceptance Agreement, the securities law restrictions applicable to this Note and any other restrictions set forth herein. At any time, Maker may prepay all or any portion of the principal amount of this Note, together with all accrued and unpaid interest through the date of prepayment (whether or not yet due on an Interest Payment Date), without penalty or premium, upon not less than five business days’ prior written notice to Lender. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to accrued and unpaid interest and then to outstanding principal. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, Maker has executed this Note as of the Issuance Date. text: EX-10.1 2 tm2629336d2_ex10-1.htm EXHIBIT 10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Cohen & Company Financial Group Cira Centre 2929 Arch Street, Suite 1703 Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19104 November 9, 2026 Lester Brafman [***] Dear Lester: This letter sets forth the terms and conditions of the cessation of your role as Chief Executive Officer of Cohen & Company, Inc., Cohen & Company, LLC, and Cohen & Company Securities, LLC, and of any of their affiliates or subsidiaries (collectively, the “Company”), effective as of the close of business on November 10, 2026 (the “Transition Date”), and the termination of your employment with the Company as of November 30, 2026 (the “Separation Date”). The terms and conditions set forth in Section 1 below will apply after your termination, regardless of whether you decide to sign this Agreement. However, the Company will not provide you with the consideration set forth in Section 2 below unless you sign and do not timely revoke this Agreement, and then re-sign and re-affirm this Agreement following the Separation Date. (Please see Section 8(c) below for what it means to revoke this Agreement). This Agreement is a very important legal document. I encourage you to read it carefully and make certain that you understand and agree with it before you sign it. You may consider this Agreement for twenty-one (21) days following your initial receipt of this Agreement whether you wish to sign this Agreement. However, you may sign it at any point within the 21-day review period, should you choose to do so. In addition, you may consider whether you wish to re-sign and re-affirm this Agreement for 21 days following the Separation Date, but you may also choose to sign this Agreement at any point within such 21-day period. Because this is a legal document, you are encouraged to review the proposed Agreement with your attorney. 1. General Terms of Termination . As noted above, regardless of whether you sign this Agreement: (a) You will cease to be the Chief Executive Officer of the Company as of the Transition Date. You submitted to the Company a notice of resignation from your role as Chief Executive Officer of the Company on November 9, 2026, effective as of the Transition Date, which the Company accepted. (b) You will be paid the balance of your base salary through the Separation Date, on the next regularly scheduled payroll date of the Company following the Separation Date. (c) Your eligibility to participate in Company-sponsored group health and dental coverage, and in the supplemental health insurance plan, as an employee of the Company, will end on the last day of the calendar month in which you are no longer employed by the Company. However, you will be eligible to continue to participate in such coverages in accordance with a federal law called the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (“COBRA”), should you elect to do so, subject to COBRA’s terms, conditions and restrictions, at your sole expense. (d) Your eligibility to participate in all other Company sponsored group benefits will end on the last day of the calendar month in which you are no longer employed by the Company. (e) Until and following the Separation Date, you must continue to comply with your common law and federal security obligations to maintain confidentiality of all Company “Proprietary Information”, as defined in Section 9(b) below. You must also continue to comply with your obligations regarding the protection of attorney-client privileged information and attorney work product, as set forth in Section 14 below. (f) In accordance with the Award Letters dated December 20, 2024, and December 19, 2025, respectively, awarded pursuant to the Cohen & Company Inc, Non-Qualified Deferred Compensation Plan (the “Deferred Compensation Plan”), you shall be paid (A) One Million and Fifty-Three Thousand, Six Hundred and Ninety-Six Dollars and No Cents ($1,053,696.00) on December 31, 2027, and (B) Three Million Seven Hundred and Seventy-Nine Thousand One Hundred and Thirty-Six Dollars ($3,779,136.00) on December 31, 2028. You acknowledge that, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Deferred Compensation Plan, you have no right to accelerate or otherwise change the timing of such payments. 2. Consideration . Provided you execute and do not timely revoke this Agreement, and it becomes effective as set forth in Section 8(c) below, and you comply with its terms, including, but not limited to, the non-disclosure, confidentiality, non-solicitation, non-interference, non-disparagement, proxy designation, inventions and return of Company property, set forth in Sections 9 to 14, and 18 below, the Company shall provide you with the following compensation and benefits specified in this Section 2 (hereinafter collectively “Separation Benefits”): (a) Effective as of the Transition Date, you will cease to be the Chief Executive Officer of the Company. Between the Transition Date and the Separation Date, you will remain employed by the Company as a Senior Advisor, and you will continue to be paid your base salary, participate in the Company’s group health and dental coverage plans, and in the supplemental health insurance plan. Your employment will terminate for all purposes on the Separation Date. (b) The Company will pay you a bonus payment of Three Million Dollars and No Cents ($3,000,000.00) within 30 days following the Separation Date in lieu of a bonus for the 2026 calendar year that you otherwise would not have been entitled to considering your Separation Date. 2 (c) The Company will pay you severance payments of: (i) within 30 days following the Separation Date, Two Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents ($2,250,000.00), which is equivalent to three times your current base salary, and (ii) on December 31, 2027, Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents ($750,000.00). (d) Should you elect to continue your health and dental insurance coverage, and/or your Supplemental Health Insurance pursuant to COBRA, the Company shall pay your premiums directly for so long as you and/or your dependents remain eligible for coverage, which should be non-taxable to you. (e) Effective as of the Separation Date, the Company will accelerate the vesting of 100% of your outstanding, unvested restricted LLC Units in Cohen & Company, LLC (i.e., 822,000 Restricted Membership Units), as more fully set forth on the Schedule of Grant Awards attached hereto as Exhibit A . At your written request by no later than the Separation Date, the Company shall repurchase 52% of these restricted LLC Units (so that you may have sufficient liquidity to pay the income tax liability resulting from such accelerated vesting). (f) Effective as of the Separation Date, the Company will accelerate the vesting of 100% of your outstanding, unvested restricted, LTIP Units in Cohen & Company, LLC (i.e., 1,605,000 LTIP Units), as more fully set forth on the Schedule of Grant Awards attached hereto as Exhibit A . On the Separation Date, in accordance with the Second Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cohen & Company, LLC, dated March 6, 2026 (the “Cohen LLC Operating Agreement”), Cohen & Company, LLC shall convert all of your LTIP Units into 1,605,000 LLC Units (the “Conversion LLC Units”). If, prior to March 31, 2027, you elect to cause Cohen & Company, LLC to redeem all such Conversion LLC Units in accordance with the Cohen LLC Operating Agreement for cash or, at the option of Cohen & Company Inc., shares of its common stock, then at least 37% of such redeemed Conversion LLC Units shall be redeemed for cash (so that you may have sufficient liquidity to pay the income tax liability resulting from such accelerated vesting). (g) You acknowledge that you have received for a de minimis amount of money founder shares in two Company sponsored SPACs, i.e., Columbus Circle 2E Sponsor Corporation LLC (“2E”) and Columbus Circle 3E Sponsor Corporation LLC (“3E”). In consideration for your execution of this Agreement, the Company agrees not to reallocate such shares, subject to the reduction noted below for 2E and potential dilution on a pro-rata basis as the Sponsor deems necessary, in accordance with the terms of the related LLC operating agreements for these two SPAC sponsors. For SPAC 2E, we are currently awaiting SEC approval of a merger proxy to close. You acknowledge that your shares in SPAC 2E have been reduced to 58,333 from the 175,000. This reduction shall be documented immediately prior to the closing via a securities assignment and joinder agreement. You also acknowledge that 3E is currently seeking a buyer and your shares in 3E may be diluted or reduced in a pro-rata amount in accordance with the terms of a business combination agreement. Share reductions may occur in either 2E or 3E as the Sponsor deems necessary. (h) In addition to the foregoing, you will receive all unpaid and accrued dividends on all such Company Restricted Membership Units and LTIP Units in accordance with all applicable award agreements and governing documents. 3 (i) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement or elsewhere, in the event of your death prior to the Separation Date or following the Separation Date but prior to the date you have received the benefits described in this Section 2, your estate will be paid and provided with the benefits described in this Section 2 on the dates described in this Section 2, subject only to your estate or legal representative signing the re-affirmation described below on your behalf. 3. General Release . (a) In consideration of the Separation Benefits and the other promises in this Agreement, you release and forever discharge, to the maximum extent permitted by law, the Company and each of the other “Releasees” (as defined below) from any and all claims, causes of action, complaints, lawsuits or liabilities of any kind (collectively “Claims”) as described below which you, your heirs, agents, administrators or executors have or may have against the Company or any of the other Releasees. (b) By agreeing to this General Release, you are waiving any and all Claims that can be waived, to the maximum extent permitted by law, which you have or may have against the Company or any of the other Releasees arising out of or relating to any conduct, matter, event or omission existing or occurring before you sign this Agreement, and any monetary or other personal relief for such Claims including but not limited to, the following: (i) any Claims having anything to do with your employment with the Company and/or any Releasee; (ii) any Claims having anything to do with the cessation of your employment with the Company and/or any Releasee; (iii) any Claims for unpaid or withheld severance, benefits, bonuses, commissions, incentive compensation, and/or compensation of any kind; (iv) any Claims under your expired employment agreement, dated September 16, 2013; (v) any Claims for reimbursements of expenses of any kind; (vi) any Claims for attorneys’ fees or costs; (vii) any Claims under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (“ERISA”); 4 (viii) any Claims of discrimination and/or harassment based on age, sex, pregnancy, race, religion, color, creed, disability, handicap, failure to accommodate, citizenship, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, genetic information or any other factor protected by Federal, State or Local law as enacted or amended (such as the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967, 29 U.S.C. § 621 et seq., Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 1981 of the Civil Rights Act of 1866, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Equal Pay Act, Section 1981 of the Civil Rights Act of 1866, the Genetic Information Non-Discrimination Act, the New York State Executive Law, New York State Human Rights Law, the New York Labor Law, the New York City Human Rights Law, the New York City Administrative Code, and any claims for retaliation under any of the foregoing laws; however, the identification of specific statutes is for purposes of example only, and the omission of any specific statute or law shall not limit the scope of this General Release in any manner. (ix) any Claims regarding leaves of absence, including, but not limited to, any Claims under the Family and Medical Leave Act or any other state or local law providing for paid or unpaid leave; (x) any Claims arising under the Immigration Reform and Control Act (“IRCA”); (xi) any Claims arising under the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (“USERRA”) or any state law governing military leave; (xii) any Claims arising under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (“WARN”) and the New York State Worker Adjustment and Retraining Act; (xiii) any Claims for violation of public policy; (xiv) any whistleblower or retaliation Claims, including but not limited to Claims arising under the New York whistleblower laws; (xv) any Claims under any state or U.S. Constitution; (xvi) any Claims under any state and/or local laws, including, but not limited to, New York and/or the local laws or ordinances of any county or city including New York City; (xvii) any Claims for emotional distress or pain and suffering; and (xviii) any other statutory, regulatory, common law or other Claims of any kind, including, but not limited to, claims for breach of contract, libel, slander, fraud, wrongful discharge, invasion of privacy, promissory estoppel, equitable estoppel and misrepresentation. (c) For purposes of this Agreement, the term “Releasees” includes: the Company, and each of its respective past, present and future parents, members, affiliates, subsidiaries, divisions, predecessors, successors, assigns, insurers, employee benefit plans and trusts, including but not limited to Cohen & Company, Inc., Cohen and Company, LLC, Cohen & Company Securities, LLC, Cohen & Company Securities Holdings, L.P., Cohen & Compagnie, SAS, Cohen & Company Financial Europe Limited S.A., Cohen & Company Financial Management, LLC, Cohen & Company Management, LLC, Cohen Principal Investing, LLC, Dekania Capital Management LLC, Dekania Investors, LLC and each of their respective past, present and future managers, directors, officers, partners, agents, employees, attorneys, representatives, consultants, associates, fiduciaries, plan sponsors, administrators and trustees of each of the foregoing and each of their respective successors and assigns. 5 (d) It is important that you understand that this General Release includes all Claims known or unknown by you, those that you may have already asserted or raised as well as those that you have never asserted or raised. (e) To the extent any Claim is not releasable, you acknowledge that the benefits set forth herein, including all of the Separation Benefits Set forth in Section 2, more than offset any monetary sums determined to be owing to you from any non-releasable claim. 4. Non-Released Claims . The General Release in Section 3 above does not apply to: (a) any Claims for vested benefits under the Company’s retirement plans; (b) any Claims to require the Company to abide by its commitments set forth in this Agreement; (c) any Claims to interpret or to determine the scope, meaning, enforceability or effect of this Agreement; (d) any Claims arising after you have signed this Agreement; (e) any Claims for worker’s compensation benefits, any Claims for unemployment compensation benefits and any other Claims that cannot be waived by a private agreement; (f) any rights to indemnification and advancement under the Company’s organizational documents, insurance policies, contracts, and/or applicable law, and coverage under the Company’s applicable D&O and other insurance policies that survive the termination of your employment. In addition, the General Release in Section 3 is subject to and limited by your Retained Rights in Section 5 below. 5. Retained Rights . (a) Regardless of whether or not you sign this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement is intended to or shall be interpreted to restrict or otherwise interfere with: (i) your obligation to testify truthfully in any forum; (ii) your right and/or obligation to contact, cooperate with, provide information to, or testify or otherwise participate in any action, investigation or proceeding of any federal, state, or local government agency, commission or entity (including, but not limited to, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”), the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), the Department of Labor (“DOL”), the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (“OSHA”), the New York State Division of Human Rights (“NYSDHR”), and the NYC Commission on Human Rights, (“collectively “Government Agencies”)); (iii) your right to disclose the details relating to the facts and circumstances or other details relating to a claim or action of discrimination, retaliation, harassment or failure to accommodate; (iv) your right and/or obligation to disclose any information or produce any documents as is required by law or legal process (v) your filing or disclosing any facts necessary to receive unemployment insurance, or other public benefits to which you are entitled; (vi) your right to speak with law enforcement, the Attorney General, or an attorney retained by you; or (vii) your right to report possible violations of federal, state or local law or regulation to any Government Agencies. 6 (b) Further, this Agreement, including the General Release in Section 3 does not prevent you from contacting or filing a charge or complaint with Government Agencies or restrict or otherwise interfere with the information you may provide to them in connection with any such contact, charge or complaint. However, the General Release does prevent you, to the maximum extent permitted by law, from obtaining any monetary or other personal relief for any of the Claims you have released in Section 3 with regard to any charge you may file or which may be filed on your behalf. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Agreement limits your right to receive an award for information provided to the SEC or any other Government Agencies. 6. Non-Admission of Wrongdoing . This Agreement shall not in any way be construed as an admission by the Company or any Releasee or any other person of any liability, or of any unlawful, discriminatory, or otherwise wrongful acts whatsoever against you or any other person. 7. Acknowledgement of Full Payments . You agree that, other than the amounts described in Sections 1(b) and 1(f) of this Agreement, the Company has paid all of the wages, fees, commissions, bonuses, incentive compensation, expense reimbursements, vacation, sick pay, holiday pay and all other employee benefits due and owing to you as a result of your employment with the Company as of the date you sign this Agreement, and that no other compensation, payments or benefits of any kind or nature is owed to you, other than as provided in this Agreement. 8. Knowing and Voluntary Waiver . Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement to the contrary: (a) You agree that this Agreement constitutes a knowing and voluntary waiver of all rights or claims you may have against the Company and the Releasees, or any of them, including, without limitation, all rights or claims arising under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967, as amended, including, but not limited to, all claims of age discrimination in employment and all claims of retaliation in violation of the ADEA . (b) Initial Signature . The Company hereby advises you to consult with an attorney prior to executing this Agreement. You acknowledge that the Company has given you a period of at least twenty-one (21) days from your initial receipt of this Agreement in which to consider this Agreement before executing this Agreement. However, you may sign this Agreement at any point within such 21-day review period. You agree that if the Company makes any changes to this Agreement, the 21-day review period shall not restart. If you execute this Agreement at any time prior to the end of the 21-day period, such early execution was a knowing and voluntary waiver of your right to consider this Agreement for 21 days. You have a period of seven days following your execution of this Agreement to revoke this Agreement by sending an email to the general counsel, Dennis Crilly ( gc@cohenandcompany.com ), stating your intent to revoke this Agreement. The email must be sent within seven (7) days of your execution of this Agreement. If the seventh day is a Sunday or federal holiday, then the email must be sent on the following business day. You will not be entitled to the Separation Benefits in Section 2 if you timely revoke this Agreement. 7 (c) Reaffirmation . In order to receive the Separation Benefits described above, you are required to re-affirm your agreement to the terms of this Agreement following the Separation Date. The Company hereby advises you to consult with an attorney prior to reaffirming this Agreement. You acknowledge that the Company has given you a period of at least twenty-one (21) days from your Separation Date to consider this Agreement before reaffirming this Agreement. However, you may reaffirm this Agreement at any point within such 21-day review period. If you reaffirm this Agreement at any time prior to the end of the 21-day period, such early execution was a knowing and voluntary waiver of your right to consider this Agreement for 21 days. You have a period of seven days following your reaffirmation of this Agreement to revoke this Agreement by sending an email to the general counsel, Dennis Crilly ( gc@cohenandcompany.com ), stating your intent to revoke this Agreement. The email must be sent within seven (7) days of your reaffirmation of this Agreement. If the seventh day is a Sunday or federal holiday, then the email must be sent on the following business day. You will not be entitled to the Separation Benefits in Section 2 if you timely revoke this Agreement. The Agreement shall become effective on the eighth day after you reaffirm this Agreement, unless you revoke it prior thereto as stated above (the “Effective Date”). 9. Non-Disclosure of the Company’s Proprietary Information . (a) You will not, without the prior written consent of the Company or applicable Releasee, either directly or indirectly, transmit or disclose to any person or entity any Proprietary Information (as defined below) or use any Proprietary Information for your own benefit or the benefit of any other person or entity, or to the detriment of the Releasees, or discuss the Company’s track record or current, past or potential client or investor information. This restriction is subject to and limited by your Retained Rights in Section 5 above. (b) Proprietary Information . For purposes of this Agreement, Proprietary Information includes, but is not limited to: (a) the identity of any clients and potential clients; (b) any information that would typically be included in the financial statements of the Company, including without limitation the amount of assets, liabilities, net worth, revenues, or net income; (c) computer software or data of any sort used, developed, or compiled by the Company; (d) information relating to the financial, operational, or organizational structure of the Company and its accounts, including without limitation marketing agreements, advisory agreements, fee-sharing arrangements, investment management account agreements, and investor subscription documents; (e) trading, investment, and order execution strategies developed, investigated, acquired, evaluated, modified, tested, or employed by the Company and information related to, or that might reasonably be expected to lead to, the development of such strategies; (f) information related to the positions, trading or investment volume, capital deployment, or transaction costs associated with the trading or investment strategies of the Company; (g) information relating to the performance of any account or investment vehicle of the Company; (h) non-public information relating to legal and professional dealings, real property, tangible property, finances, business, investment activities, and other affairs of the Company; (i) information regarding the identity or background of individuals considered for employment by the Company; (j) any intellectual property rights acquired or developed by the Company, whether or not patentable or copyrightable, including all business plans, projects, partnerships, know-how, technical information, inventions, designs, configurations, ideas, concepts, processes, procedures, operations, research and development plans, pricing information, and business, operational, and marketing plans; (k) confidential and/or proprietary information learned from the Company’s investors, potential investors, advisory clients, clients, potential clients, existing and potential affiliates, subsidiaries and other related entities, suppliers, contracting parties, and other third parties with which the Company has business relations or potential business relations; and (l) any and all other data or information relating to the operations and business of the Company that is not known generally by and readily accessible to the public. Proprietary Information shall not include information which is generally known by or readily accessible to the public through no fault you or anyone acting in concert with you. 8 (c) Track Records . You acknowledge that track records and other performance information of accounts managed by the Company, including without limitation the performance of any sectors and individual securities or other investment interests or vehicles managed by the Company, are the exclusive property of the Company. Without the prior written consent of the Company’s General Counsel, you will not: (i) represent to anyone within or outside of the Company that you were responsible for the performance or track records of these accounts; (ii) disclose investment performance information to anyone other than current or potential investors and only after receiving the permission of the Company; or (iii) otherwise utilize the investment performance of the Company or information related thereto. (d) Discussions Regarding the Company . Subject to your retained rights in Section 5 of this Agreement, without the prior written consent of the Company’s General Counsel, you are prohibited from having any conversations regarding the Company’s clients, potential clients, investors or potential investors with the media, any regulator, or any regulatory agency, other than as required by law or to legal, tax and accounting professionals who require the information to provide professional services to you. (e) Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016 . Nothing in this Agreement is intended to or shall be interpreted to prohibit disclosure of information to the limited extent permitted by and in accordance with the federal Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016 (“DTSA ”) . Stated otherwise, disclosures that are protected by the DTSA as follows do not violate this Agreement. The DTSA provides that: “(1) An individual shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any Federal or State trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that – (A) is made – (i) in confidence to a Federal, State, or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney; and (ii) solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or (B) is made in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal.” The DTSA further provides that: “(2) An individual who files a lawsuit for retaliation by an employer for reporting a suspected violation of law may disclose the trade secret to the attorney of the individual and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding, if the individual – (A) files any document containing the trade secret under seal; and (B) does not disclose the trade secret, except pursuant to court order.” This provision is subject to Section 9(f) below. (f) Demand for Disclosure of Proprietary Information . In the event you receive a request or demand, orally, in writing, electronically or otherwise, for the disclosure or production of Proprietary Information, you must notify immediately Dennis Crilly at gc@cohenandcompany.com A copy of the request or demand, as well as any and all documents potentially responsive to the request or demand, shall be included with the written notification. You shall wait a minimum of ten (10) days (or the maximum time permitted by such legal process, if less) after sending the letter before making a disclosure or production to give the Company time to determine whether the disclosure or production involves Proprietary Information, in which event the Company may seek to prohibit and/or restrict the production and/or disclosure and/or to obtain a protective order with regard thereto. This restriction is subject to and limited by your Retained Rights in Section 5 above and does not apply to requests or demands from government officials or investigators, if such government officials or investigators affirmatively instruct or request that you not inform the Company of the demand or request for information. 9 (g) Material Non-Public Information; Securities Law Compliance . You acknowledge that, by virtue of your position as Chief Executive Officer, you are in possession of, or may have had access to, material non-public information (“MNPI”) concerning the Company, Cohen & Company, Inc., 2E and 3E (as defined above), any other Company-sponsored SPAC, and their respective clients, counterparties and business combination targets. You agree that you will not, directly or indirectly, purchase, sell or otherwise trade in, or recommend or tip any other person to trade in, any securities of any such entity while in possession of MNPI, and that you will not disclose MNPI to any person except as permitted by Section 5 above. You further agree that you will continue to comply with the Company’s Insider Trading Policy (including its blackout periods and pre-clearance requirements) until the later of (i) the opening of the first trading window following the Separation Date and (ii) the date on which any MNPI in your possession has been publicly disclosed or is no longer material. You acknowledge that you remain responsible for complying with all applicable federal and state securities laws following the Separation Date, including, to the extent applicable, Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), and the rules thereunder (including the filing of any required Form 4 or Form 5 and the short-swing profit rules for the six-month period following the Separation Date), Sections 13(d) and 13(g) of the Exchange Act, Rule 144 under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Regulation FD. You agree to cooperate with the Company in connection with any required public disclosure or filing relating to your separation or your holdings of Company securities, and to promptly provide any information reasonably requested by the Company for such purposes. Nothing in this Paragraph 9(g) limits your Retained Rights in Section 5 above. 10. Non-Solicitation and Non-Interference . In consideration for the Separation Benefits, you agree to the following post-employment restrictions, as the terms “Person”, “Competitive Business” and “Restricted Client” are respectively defined in Sections 10(d) through (f) below: (a) You acknowledge that: (i) in your position, you had access to sensitive, financial information regarding the Company and persons and entities with a contractual, business, or professional relationship with the Company, including its clients, potential clients, investors and potential investors; (ii) the Company’s business currently spans the world; (iii) your position as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer brought you into close contact with Proprietary Information of the Company and its clients, potential clients, investors and potential investors, the benefit of Company’s goodwill, customer relationships and specialized training, among other forms of valuable consideration; (iv) your work for the Company was performed and/or could have been performed from places around the world and the Company’s clients are located around the world; (v) the agreements and covenants contained in this Section 11 are essential to and no greater than necessary to protect the legitimate business interests of the Company; (vi) the Company would not provide the Separation Benefits but for such agreement and covenants; and (vii) the covenants in this Section 10 are ancillary to or part of an otherwise enforceable separation agreement. 10 (b) You agree that for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Separation Date, you shall not, directly or indirectly, individually or on behalf of any other Person or other entity, in any capacity (as an employee, independent contractor, consultant, owner, partner or otherwise) (i) induce, solicit, or attempt to influence any actively sought, prospective partners, members, employees, and independent contractors of the Company with whom you had material contact while employed not to establish a partnership, employment or contractual relationship with the Company; or (ii) in any way interfere with the relationship between the Company and any of its partners, members, employees or independent contractors. (c) Additionally, you agree that for a period of twelve (12) months following the Separation Date you shall not, directly or indirectly, individually or on behalf of any other Person or other entity, in any capacity (as an employee, independent contractor, consultant, owner, partner or otherwise): (i) interfere with or adversely affect the contractual, business, or professional relationship between the Company and any Restricted Clients by soliciting, inducing, causing, or requesting such client to cease doing business, not do business, reduce or otherwise limit its business relationship with the Company; (ii) solicit, aid or induce any Restricted Client to enter into a business relationship with another Person other than the Company, for services or products in which the Company was engaged with such client, or assist or aid any other Persons in a Competitive Business in identifying or soliciting any such Restricted Client for any services or products in which the Company was engaged with such Restricted Client; (iii) induce, solicit, or attempt to influence, any current partner, member, employee or independent contractor of the Company to terminate, diminish or materially alter their partnership, employment or contractual relationship with the Company; or (iv) induce, solicit, or attempt to influence any vendor of the Company to terminate, diminish or materially alter their relationship with the Company or any of its affiliates. (d) The term “Person” shall mean an individual, a partnership, a corporation, a limited liability company, an association, a joint stock company, a trust, a joint venture, an unincorporated organization, or a governmental or any other form of entity. 11 (e) The term “Competitive Business” shall mean any other business or organization (including financial services organizations and sponsors of SPACs) anywhere in the world which provides services and/or products of a nature substantially similar to those provided by the Company during your employment with the Company, including, but not limited to, services and/or products relating to Advisory, Capital Markets, SPACs, and PIPE deals or which otherwise directly competes with the Company. (f) The term “Restricted Client” shall mean any (i) client of the Company with whom you had personal contact, whose relationship you managed on behalf of the Company, or regarding which you have, or had at any point during the course of your employment with the Company, Proprietary Information or other confidential information; and (ii) prospective client of the Company with whom you had personal contact, whose relationship you managed on behalf of the Company, or regarding which you have, or had during the last twelve (12) months of your employment with the Company, Proprietary Information or other confidential information. 11. Return of Company Property . You shall, as of the Separation Date, return to the Company, and retain no copies of, any and all Company equipment, devices, and other property provided to you by the Company or otherwise owned by the Company (including, but not limited to, access cards, keys, laptops, phones, hard drives, thumb drives), without resetting or wiping any such Company equipment or devices, and all passwords and other information necessary to access Company equipment, devices, or other property) and any and all Company documents (whether hard copy/printed or electronic) reflecting Proprietary Information or otherwise relating to the Company’s business operations, clients, prospective clients, suppliers, vendors, etc., regardless of where or in what format such items are kept or prepared. 12. Inventions . (a) Disclosure . You shall disclose fully, promptly and in writing to the Company any and all inventions, discoveries, improvements, modifications, ideas, formula, processes, know-how, methods, trademarks and other works (hereinafter “Inventions”), whether or not suitable for patent or copyright, which you have conceived, made, discovered, enhanced, developed or reduced to practice, solely or jointly with others, while employed by the Company and which (i) relate to the businesses, work or activities of the Company, or (ii) result from or are suggested your having carried out your duties relating to your employment with the Company or from or by any information that you may have received as an employee of the Company. (b) Assignment and Assistance . You hereby assign, transfer and convey to the Company all of your right, title and interest existing now or in the future in and to any and all such Inventions, including any rights under domestic or foreign patent law, trademark law, industrial rights design law, semiconductor chip and mark work protection law, trade secret law and any and all similar proprietary rights, however denominated, and any and all continuations, continuations-in-part, divisions, renewals, reissue, re-examinations, extensions and/or restorations thereof, now or hereafter in force and effect. To the extent any of the rights, title and interest in and to Inventions cannot be assigned by you to Company, you hereby grant to the Company an exclusive, royalty-free, transferable, irrevocable, worldwide license (with rights to sublicense through multiple tiers of sublicensees) to practice such non-assignable rights, title and interest. You agree to take all such actions as may be requested by the Company at any time and with respect to any such Inventions, to confirm or evidence such assignment, transfer or conveyance. Furthermore, at any time and from time to time, upon the request of the Company, you shall execute and deliver to the Company, any and all instruments, documents and papers, give evidence and do any and all other acts that, in the opinion of counsel for the Company, are or may be necessary or desirable to document such assignment, transfer, or conveyance or to enable the Company to file and prosecute applications for and to acquire, maintain and enforce any and all patents, trademark registrations under United States or foreign law with respect to any such Inventions, or to obtain any extension, validation, reissue, continuance or renewal of any such patent or trademark. The Company shall be responsible for the preparation of any such instruments, documents and papers and for the prosecution of any such proceedings and shall reimburse you for all reasonable expenses incurred by you in compliance with the provisions of this Section. 12 (c) Work Made for Hire . You agree that any work product that arose out of the employment relationship (“Work Product”) is a work made for hire exclusively for the Company as that term is defined the Copyright Act of 1976, as amended (17 U.S.C. Section 101) and Company shall be the “author” of the Work Product within the meaning of the Copyright Act. Such Work Product shall be and remain the exclusive property of the Company and the Company shall have the right to use such Work Product for any purpose without any additional compensation to you. In the event that any Work Product shall not be deemed to be a work made for hire exclusively for the Company under the Copyright Act, you hereby transfer and assign to the Company all right, title and interest in and to said Work Product, including any and all copyrights therein throughout the world, together with any moral rights therein. You shall cooperate with Company to take all actions reasonably necessary to ensure such rights are so assigned. You irrevocably waive in favor of the Company and the Company’s successors, licensees and assigns, all their moral rights in and to all Work Product throughout the universe. 13. Non-Disparagement . You agree to refrain from making any defamatory or disparaging remarks, whether directly or indirectly, orally or in writing, through any medium, that would disparage, defame, impugn or otherwise damage or assail the reputation, integrity, or professionalism of the Company or the Releasees, or regarding the quality of the Company’s products and/or its services. You further agree to refrain from making knowingly false statements or statements made with reckless disregard for the truth about the Company or any Releasee. This restriction is subject to and limited by your Retained Rights in Section 5 above. 14. No Waiver of Attorney-Client Privileged Information and Attorney Work Product . You acknowledge and agree that in your role as Chief Executive Officer for the Company, you were privy to attorney-client privileged advice and had access to attorney work product with respect to the Company’s internal and external counsel. You acknowledge and agree that the attorney-client privilege belongs to the Company, and you are not authorized to use or disclose any information protected by the attorney-client privilege or the attorney work product doctrine with respect to the Company. Nothing in this Agreement is intended to permit you to use or disclose any attorney-client privileged information or any attorney work product with respect to the Company or to any of the Releasees, without explicit prior written consent of the Company’s General Counsel or their designee or without a court order issued after notice to the Company and an opportunity for the Company to participate. 13 15. Remedy for Breach . You acknowledge and agree that, in view of the nature of the business in which the Company is engaged, as well as your position as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer: (i) the restrictions contained in Sections 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 of this Agreement are reasonable in all respects, including in time, geography and scope, and necessary to protect the legitimate interests of the Company; (ii) any violation of these restrictions would result in irreparable injury to the Company for which monetary damages would not provide an adequate remedy; and (iii) these restrictions will not preclude you from earning a living. You therefore acknowledge and agree that, if you breach or threaten to breach any of the restrictions in Sections 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 the Company will have available, in addition to any other right or remedy, the right to obtain injunctive and equitable relief, as well as to obtain damages and an equitable accounting of all earnings, profits and other benefits arising from such violation. You further agree that a bond or other security of not more than the amount of Five Thousand Dollars and No Cents ($5,000.00) shall be required from the Company in obtaining such equitable relief. If a court or other deciding body determines that you have violated any of the restrictions contained in Sections 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 the restrictive period shall be tolled from the time of the commencement of the violation until such time as the violation shall be cured by you. In connection with any Claims related to this provision, each party shall be responsible for their own attorney’s fees and shall bear their own costs and expenses. 16. Cooperation . You agree to cooperate with the Company or any Releasees in connection with any claims, complaints, charges, actions, lawsuits or similar proceedings which may be brought against the Company or any Releasees and which the Company deems your cooperation necessary. You will be available to cooperate fully with the Company’s counsel or other representatives as needed, unless otherwise required by law. You also agree to promptly notify the Company’s General Counsel in writing of any contacts by an attorney or third party relating to legal proceedings commenced or to be commenced against the Company or any of the Releasees. In the event your cooperation is sought pursuant to this Section 16, the Company shall reimburse you solely for reasonable pre-approved travel expenses incurred by you as a result of such cooperation (including reasonable lodging and meals, upon submission of receipts). You agree not to cooperate directly or indirectly in any way with any party bringing a claim against the Company or any Releasee, unless your action is required by law or governmental agency, in which case you shall promptly give notice to the Company of such legal requirement, so that the Company or its designee may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. Notice is not required where the action is required by a governmental agency that directs you to refrain from notifying the Company or in connection with a matter before the SEC. This restriction is subject to and limited by your Retained Rights in Section 5 above. 17. Resignation from Company Boards . You agree that you shall immediately resign from the Board of Directors of Cohen & Company Financial (Europe) Ltd, Board of Managers of Cohen & Company, LLC any other board seat you hold at any affiliated or related entity of the Company. 18. Provision of Proxy Designation . Effective as of the Separation Date, you hereby grant to Cohen & Company, Inc. an irrevocable proxy, coupled with an interest, to vote all of your membership interests in Cohen & Company, LLC that you now hold or later acquire, on all matters on which such membership interest are entitled to vote, and you agree to execute any further instrument reasonably requested by the Company to evidence such proxy. This proxy shall be permanent and perpetual and shall survive any transfer of such units to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the operating agreement of Cohen & Company, LLC. 14 19. Adequacy of Consideration . You acknowledge and agree that the Separation Benefits reflected in Section 2 above are not required to be provided by any policy, plan, or prior agreement and constitutes adequate consideration to support the General Release in Section 3 and fully compensates you for the Claims you are releasing and constitutes adequate consideration for your commitments in Sections 9 to 14, 18 and elsewhere, in this Agreement. For purposes of this Section, “consideration” means something of value to which you are not already entitled. 20. Entire Contract/Severability/Modification . This Agreement sets forth the entire agreement between you and the Company and supersedes in its entirety all prior agreements, understandings or representations with the Company and/or any Releasee relating to the subject matter hereof. Should any provision of this Agreement be found to be overbroad, or declared or determined by a court to be illegal or invalid, the court shall have the power to modify this Agreement so that it conforms with prevailing law and the validity of the remaining parts, terms or provisions shall not be affected thereby. You represent that in executing this Agreement, you do not rely on any statement or fact not set forth herein. This Agreement may not be modified except by a writing signed by both parties hereto. 21. Governing Law . The parties agree that this Agreement will be construed under the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of law provisions of the state in which any action may be filed that would result in the application of the laws of another jurisdiction. The parties specifically acknowledge that this Agreement has been negotiated between the parties at arms’ length and that you have been represented by independent legal counsel of your own choosing in connection with the negotiation of all terms of this Agreement, including the governing law and forum provisions and that your independent legal counsel has informed you of the impact of the governing law and forum provisions. The parties’ further consent and agree that the federal and state courts of New York, New York will have exclusive jurisdiction over any Claims, disputes and controversies arising from this Agreement. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO A JURY TRIAL IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT. 22. Section 409A . (a) All of the payments and benefits payable pursuant to this Agreement are intended to comply with, or be exempt from, section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (“Section 409A”), to the extent the requirements of Section 409A are applicable hereto, and the provisions of this Agreement shall be construed and administered in a manner consistent with that intention. For purposes of Section 409A of the Code, each payment made under this Agreement shall be designated as a “separate payment” within the meaning of Section 409A, (b) If you are a “specified employee” within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(i) as of the date of your Separation Date, you shall not be entitled to any payment or benefit to the extent that any such payment would constitute “nonqualified deferred compensation” (if at all) within the meaning of Section 409A until the earlier of: (i) the date which is six (6) months after such Separation Date for any reason other than death; or (ii) the date of Employee’s death. The provisions of this Section shall only apply if, and to the extent, required to avoid the imputation of any tax, penalty or interest pursuant to Section 409A. Any amounts otherwise payable to Employee upon or in the six (6) month period following Employee’s Separation Date that are not so paid by reason of this Section shall be paid (without interest) as soon as practicable after the date that is six (6) months after Employee’s Separation Date (or, if earlier, as soon as practicable after the date of Employee’s death). 15 (c) To the extent that any reimbursement pursuant to this Agreement is taxable to Employee, Employee shall provide the Company with documentation of the related expenses promptly so as to facilitate the timing of the reimbursement payment contemplated by this Section, and any reimbursement payment due to Employee pursuant to such provision shall be paid to Employee on or before the last day of Employee’s taxable year following the taxable year in which the related expense was incurred. Such reimbursement obligations pursuant to this Agreement are not subject to liquidation or exchange for another benefit and the amount of such benefits that Employee receives in one taxable year shall not affect the amount of such benefits that Employee receives in any other taxable year. (d) In no event shall the Company be required to pay you any “gross-up” or other payment with respect to any taxes or penalties imposed under Section 409A with respect to any benefit paid to you hereunder except to the extent any such taxes or penalties result from the Company’s gross negligence or willful misconduct. The Company agrees to take any reasonable steps requested by you to avoid adverse tax consequences to you as a result of any benefit to you hereunder being subject to Section 409A, provided that you shall, if requested, reimburse the Company for any incremental costs (other than incidental costs) associated with taking such steps. 23. Headings . This Agreement will not be construed against any party on the ground that it was the drafter of the Agreement or any particular provision. All captions and headings herein contained are inserted for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. 24. Notices . Any notice to be given hereunder will be deemed sufficient if given in writing and delivered either personally, courier or overnight delivery service all with proof of delivery, or if sent via email to the Company at dcrilly@cohenandcompany.com, or if sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Company to the attention of the General Counsel and to you at the address set forth above. 25. Acknowledgement . You expressly acknowledge and agree that you have carefully read this Agreement; that you fully understand the terms, conditions and significance of this Agreement; that the Company has advised you of your right to consult with an attorney concerning this Agreement; that you had a period of at least 21 days to review this Agreement with an attorney before executing it; that you had a period of 7 days following execution of the Agreement to revoke this Agreement; and that you have executed this Agreement voluntarily, knowingly and with such advice of an attorney as you have deemed appropriate. [Signature page follows.] 16 Please sign where indicated below and return this Agreement to the Company as set forth above. Sincerely, COHEN & COMPANY, INC. , on behalf of itself and Cohen & Company, LLC, Cohen & Company Securities, LLC and each of their affiliates and subsidiaries By: /s/ Daniel Cohen Name: Daniel Cohen Title: Chairman Agreed to and accepted by: /s/ Lester Brafman Lester Brafman Date: November 9, 2026
