title: HUBSPOT INC
text: EX-10.1 2 d77303dex101.htm EX-10.1 EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 November 12, 2026 Yamini Rangan [***] [***] Dear Yamini, The purpose of this letter agreement (this “ Agreement ”) is to confirm the terms of your separation from HubSpot, Inc. (“ HubSpot ” or the “ Company ”) (collectively, the “ Parties ”). The payments and benefits described in Section 2 of this Agreement are provided to assist you with your transition from the Company and are in exchange for the obligations you are accepting which are described in this Agreement. HubSpot’s obligations under this Agreement are contingent on (1) your timely signing of this Agreement and this Agreement becoming effective, and (2) your compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. Please return the signed Agreement via DocuSign within twenty-one (21) days of the date of this Agreement. This Agreement will be effective the day following the conclusion of your seven-day revocation period described in Section 4(d) (the “ Effective Date ”). 1 . Termination as Chief Executive Officer and Separation from Employment As of November 12, 2026 (the “ Transition Date ”), you will no longer serve as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, Principal Executive Officer, and President. Your final day of employment is December 1, 2026 (the “ Separation Date ”), which shall be the Date of Termination for purposes of any payments due to you pursuant to the HubSpot, Inc. Executive Severance Plan (the “ Executive Severance Plan ”). This is a termination by the Company without Cause under the Executive Severance Plan. You will continue to have access to Slack through November 13, 2026 and to your Company email address through the Separation Date. Between the Transition Date and the Separation Date, you may use paid time off in accordance with the Company’s policies. Prior to the Transition Date, you will continue to be covered under the Company’s existing directors and officers liability insurance policy (the “ D&O Policy ”) on the same basis as immediately prior to the date of this Agreement, consistent with your role as an executive officer of the Company. Effective as of the Transition Date, the Company will add you as an individually named insured under the D&O Policy, and will maintain such individual coverage for you through the Separation Date, in each case subject to the terms, conditions, and exclusions of the D&O Policy as in effect from time to time. 2 . Severance and Other Benefits . In exchange for: (i) your execution and non-revocation of, and compliance with, this Agreement, and (ii) your execution and non-revocation of the Certificate attached as Exhibit A after the Separation Date within the timeframe set forth therein, as outlined in Section 6 of the Executive Severance Plan, HubSpot will provide you with the below (collectively, the “ Severance Benefits ”). 1 (a) HubSpot will pay you an amount equal to $1,336,712.33, which represents the sum of (i) your Base Salary (as defined in the Executive Severance Plan) and (ii) your pro-rated Target Bonus (as defined in the Executive Severance Plan) through the Separation Date, less applicable deductions and withholdings (the “ Severance Amount ”). HubSpot will pay you the Severance Amount in accordance with HubSpot’s regular payroll practices in substantially equal installments, over twelve (12) months following the Separation Date (the “ Severance Period ”), commencing with the first regular payroll date following the Certificate Effective Date (as defined in Exhibit A), but in any event no later than sixty (60) days following the Certificate Effective Date; provided, however, that if the period between the Separation Date and the Certificate Effective Date spans two taxable years, the first payment shall be made in the second taxable year. (b) Your current coverage under HubSpot’s medical and dental insurance plans will automatically continue until December 31, 2026. If you execute, do not revoke, and comply with this Agreement, then, subject to the conditions outlined in the Executive Severance Plan, HubSpot will pay to the group health plan provider or the COBRA provider a monthly payment equal to 100% of your monthly COBRA health and dental insurance monthly COBRA premiums until the earliest of (i) the 12-month anniversary of the Separation Date; (ii) the date that you become eligible for group medical plan benefits under another employer’s group medical plan; or (iii) the cessation of your health continuation rights under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (“ COBRA ”), after which you may, at your own expense, continue participation in COBRA for the balance of time provided by the statute (provided, however, the “qualifying event” under COBRA shall be deemed to have occurred on the Separation Date). If you do not sign and return this Agreement, you may, at your own expense, continue to participate in HubSpot’s medical and dental insurance plans, to the same extent that HubSpot provides such insurance to its current employees, by completing the appropriate forms to enroll under COBRA. You will receive the COBRA forms in the mail, and you have 60 days from the Separation Date to submit them. The Separation Date is the date of the “qualifying event” under COBRA. (c) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any applicable Equity Award (as defined in the Executive Severance Plan) agreement or Company equity incentive plan, all Equity Awards held by you that would have otherwise vested during the 12-month period following the Separation Date, including but not limited to all Equity Awards scheduled to vest on December 1, 2027, (with any performance-based Equity Awards being deemed earned at the target level of performance) shall immediately accelerate and become fully vested and exercisable or nonforfeitable as of the Accelerated Vesting Date (as defined in the Executive Severance Plan); provided that in order to effectuate the accelerated vesting contemplated by this Section 2(c), the unvested portion of your Equity Awards that would otherwise terminate or be forfeited on the Separation Date will be delayed until the earlier of (i) the Effective Date of this Agreement (at which time acceleration will occur) or (ii) the date that this Agreement can no longer become fully effective (at which time the unvested portion of your Equity Awards will terminate and be forfeited). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no additional vesting of your Equity Awards will occur during the period between the Separation Date and the Accelerated Vesting Date. 2 3 . Equity Awards . Other than as set forth in Section 2(c) of this Agreement, the terms, rights and conditions of your Equity Awards are governed by HubSpot Inc. 2024 Stock Option and Incentive Plan (the “ Plan ”) or the applicable Prior Plan (as defined in the Plan), as applicable, and any award agreements or other documents that you signed for any stock options, restricted stock units or other Equity Awards under the Plan or the Prior Plans. Any Equity Awards scheduled to vest on December 1, 2026, will vest on such date. 4 . Release and Review . (a) Release . In exchange for the Severance Benefits, which you acknowledge you would not otherwise be entitled to receive, you hereby fully, forever, irrevocably and unconditionally release, remise and discharge HubSpot, including, but not limited to, its current and former officers, directors, stockholders, agents, plan administrators, attorneys and employees and its corporate affiliates, subsidiaries and parent companies (collectively, the “ Released Parties ”) from all claims, charges, complaints, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, rights, debts, sums of money, costs, accounts, covenants, contracts, agreements, promises, doings, omissions, damages, executions, obligations, liabilities, and expenses (including attorneys’ fees and costs) of every kind and nature arising before and up to the date you sign this Agreement related to your employment with or separation from HubSpot, including, but not limited to, (1) all employment discrimination claims under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (42 U.S.C. §2000e et seq.), the Massachusetts Fair Employment Practices Act (also known as Chapter 151B), the Americans With Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C., §12101 et seq.), the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993 (29 U.S.C. §2601 et seq.), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (“ ADEA ”), the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act (“ OWBPA ”), the California Family Rights Act and all other similar applicable federal and state statutes, all as amended; (2) all claims arising out of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. §1681 et seq.), the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA, 29 U.S.C. §1001 et seq.) and the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (29 U.S.C. §2101 et seq.), all as amended; (3) all common law claims including, but not limited to, actions in tort, defamation and breach of contract; (4) all claims related to wages, hours, whistleblowing and the terms and conditions of employment, including, but not limited to, the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Massachusetts Payment of Wages Law (Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 149, §§ 148, 150), Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 149 in its entirety and Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 151 in its entirety (including, without limitation, the sections concerning payment of wages, minimum wage and overtime), the California Labor Code, the California Workers’ Compensation Act, the Massachusetts Earned Sick Time Law and the Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave law, all as amended; (5) all claims to any non-vested ownership interest in HubSpot, whether contractual or otherwise, including, but not limited to, claims to unvested Equity Awards (other than those Equity Awards that accelerate and vest pursuant to Section 2(c) of this Agreement); and (6) any claim or damage arising out of your employment with or separation from HubSpot (including a claim for retaliation) under any common law theory or any federal, state or local statute or ordinance not expressly referenced above. You represent that you have not filed nor are there any pending charges or lawsuits filed by you against any Released Party. 3 California Civil Code Section 1542 . You acknowledge that you have been advised to consult with legal counsel and are familiar with the provisions of California Civil Code Section 1542, a statute that otherwise prohibits the release of unknown claims, which provides as follows: A GENERAL RELEASE DOES NOT EXTEND TO CLAIMS THAT THE CREDITOR OR RELEASING PARTY DOES NOT KNOW OR SUSPECT TO EXIST IN HIS OR HER FAVOR AT THE TIME OF EXECUTING THE RELEASE AND THAT, IF KNOWN BY HIM OR HER, WOULD HAVE MATERIALLY AFFECTED HIS OR HER SETTLEMENT WITH THE DEBTOR OR RELEASED PARTY. You, being aware of said code section, agree to expressly waive any rights you may have thereunder, as well as under any other statute or common law principles of similar effect. (b) Company Release . In consideration of your promises under this Agreement, effective as of the Effective Date, except for the Excluded Claims (as defined below), HubSpot, its subsidiaries, and their respective successors and assigns (collectively, the “ Company Releasing Parties ”) hereby fully, forever, irrevocably and unconditionally releases, remises and discharges you and your heirs, executors, administrators and assigns from all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, damages, liabilities, obligations, costs and expenses (including attorneys’ fees and costs), of every kind and nature, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, that Company Releasing Parties has or may have arising out of or relating to your employment with, service to, or separation from HubSpot on or before the date HubSpot signs this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company Releasing Parties do not release or discharge any claims against you for willful misconduct, fraud, breach of fiduciary duty of loyalty, criminal acts or conduct, embezzlement, or misappropriation of trade secrets or proprietary information (the “ Excluded Claims ”). HubSpot represents that it is not aware, as of the date it signs this Agreement, of any facts sufficient to support an Excluded Claim. For the avoidance of doubt, the release does not apply to any Excluded Claim asserted by a stockholder derivatively on behalf of the Company Releasing Parties. HubSpot acknowledges that it has been advised to consult with legal counsel, is familiar with California Civil Code Section 1542 as quoted in Section 4(a), and expressly waives all rights under that section and any statute or common law principle of similar effect with respect to the claims released by the Company Releasing Parties (except for the Excluded Claims). (c) Neither Party’s release under this Agreement releases any claim to enforce this Agreement, any claim arising after the applicable releasing Party signs this Agreement, or any claim that cannot lawfully be released. Your release does not waive your rights to vested benefits, the Severance Benefits, or indemnification, advancement of expenses or coverage under applicable directors’ and officers’ liability insurance. 4 (d) Review and Rescission Period . Because you are at least forty (40) years of age, you have specific rights under the ADEA and OWBPA, which prohibit discrimination on the basis of age. The release in this Section 4 is intended to release any claim you may have against HubSpot alleging discrimination on the basis of age under the ADEA, OWBPA and other laws. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the release in this Section 4 does not cover rights or claims under the ADEA that arise from acts or omissions that occur after the date you sign this Agreement. It is the Company’s desire and intent to make certain that you fully understand the provisions and effects of this Agreement. To that end, the Company hereby advises you in writing to consult with legal counsel prior to signing this Agreement for the purpose of reviewing the terms of this Agreement. Consistent with the provisions of the OWBPA, the Company is providing you with twenty-one (21) days to consider and accept the terms of this Agreement by signing below and returning it to the Company. You may use as much of this 21-day period as you see fit. However, to the extent that you decide to sign the Agreement prior to the expiration of this 21-day period, such decision was knowing and voluntary on your part. You agree that this time period has provided you with ample opportunity to review the terms of the Agreement and to seek legal counsel. You agree that any changes to this Agreement, whether material or immaterial, will not restart the running of this 21-day period. In addition, you may rescind your assent to this Agreement if, within seven (7) days after you sign this Agreement, you deliver a notice of rescission to the Company ATTN: Chief People Officer , at 2 Canal Park, Cambridge, MA 02141. To be effective, such rescission must be hand delivered or postmarked within the seven-day period and sent by trackable mail courier (e.g., FedEx or USPS certified mail, return receipt requested). (e) Limitation . Nothing contained in this Agreement, any other agreement with the Company or any Company policy limits your ability, with or without notice to the Company, to: (i) file a charge or complaint with any federal, state or local governmental agency or commission (a “ Government Agency ”), including without limitation, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the National Labor Relations Board or the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”); (ii) communicate with any Government Agency or otherwise participate in any investigation or proceeding that may be conducted by any Government Agency, including by providing non-privileged documents or information; (iii) exercise any rights under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act, which are available to non-supervisory employees, including assisting co-workers with or discussing any employment issue as part of engaging in concerted activities for the purpose of mutual aid or protection; (iv) discuss or disclose information about unlawful acts in the workplace, such as harassment or discrimination or any other conduct that you have reason to believe is unlawful; or (v) testify truthfully in a legal proceeding. Any such communications and disclosures must not violate applicable law and the information disclosed must not have been obtained through a communication that was subject to the attorney-client privilege (unless disclosure of that information would otherwise be permitted consistent with such privilege or applicable law). If a Government Agency or any other third party pursues any claim on your behalf, you waive any right to monetary or other individualized relief (either individually or as part of any collective or class action), but the Company will not limit any right you may have to receive an award pursuant to the whistleblower provisions of any applicable law or regulation for providing information to the SEC or any other Government Agency. 5 5 . Post-Termination Obligations . Your obligations under any confidentiality, assignment of inventions and/or restrictive covenant agreements that you entered into with the Company and any other policies and/or agreements with continuing obligations will survive in accordance with their terms. Notwithstanding your confidentiality and nondisclosure obligations, you are hereby advised as follows pursuant to the Defend Trade Secrets Act: “An individual shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any Federal or State trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that (A) is made (i) in confidence to a Federal, State, or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney; and (ii) solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or (B) is made in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal. An individual who files a lawsuit for retaliation by an employer for reporting a suspected violation of law may disclose the trade secret to the attorney of the individual and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding, if the individual (A) files any document containing the trade secret under seal; and (B) does not disclose the trade secret, except pursuant to court order.” 6 . Return of HubSpot Property . You represent and affirm that you will return to HubSpot all Company property and equipment in your possession or control no later than the Separation Date, including, but not limited to, computer equipment (such as, but not limited to, computer hardware, software and printers, wireless handheld devices and cellular phones), customer information, customer lists, employee lists, Company files, notes, contracts, records, business plans, financial information, specifications, computer-recorded information, software, tangible property, identification badges and keys and any other materials of any kind that contain or embody any proprietary or confidential material of HubSpot (and all copies of these materials). You agree to leave intact all electronic Company documents, including those that you developed or helped develop during your employment. You also agree to cancel all accounts for your benefit, if any, in HubSpot’s name such as, but not limited to, credit cards, telephone charge cards, cellular phone accounts and computer accounts. 7 . Business Expenses and Compensation . You acknowledge that all outstanding business expenses incurred in connection with your employment with HubSpot will be submitted for payment within 30 days of the Separation Date. 8 . Non-Disparagement. Subject to Section 4(e) of this Agreement, you agree not to make any false, disparaging, derogatory or defamatory statements (whether in person, electronically, on social media or otherwise) in public or in private to any party regarding HubSpot or any of the other Released Parties, or regarding HubSpot’s business affairs, business prospects and financial condition. HubSpot and the members of the Board of Directors (the “ Board ”) agree not to make any public, official statement that is false, disparaging, derogatory or defamatory (whether in person, electronically, on social media or otherwise) regarding you. HubSpot shall further instruct its Board members and the Company Executive Leadership Team not to make any such statements, whether in public or in private. These restrictions cover statements to all third parties, such as, 6 but not limited to, media outlets, industry groups, financial institutions and current and former employees, consultants, clients and customers of HubSpot. Nothing in this Section prohibits either Party, or any individual subject to this Section, from giving truthful testimony, making truthful statements required by law, subpoena or other legal process, communicating with or participating in proceedings before any Government Agency, making disclosures protected by applicable law, making truthful statements reasonably necessary to enforce this Agreement, and shall not prohibit any Board member or member of the Company Executive Leadership Team from making statements in good faith for legitimate business purposes, including in connection with the discharge of their fiduciary duties, Board deliberations, the evaluation of management or business performance, or communications with legal counsel, auditors, regulators or other persons having a legitimate business need to receive such statements, provided that the Board member or member of the Company Executive Leadership Team reasonably believes the statements to be accurate and appropriate for the purpose and audience. 9 . Cooperation. To the extent that HubSpot determines you possess relevant information, you agree to provide such reasonable cooperation and assistance as may be requested in good faith by the Company and at mutually convenient times with respect to the investigation and handling of any threatened, pending or future litigation, regulatory proceeding, investigation, administrative or other hearing, trial or proceeding initiated by Company or any other person, entity or governmental body against Company, its affiliates, subsidiaries and/or related entities. Cooperation and assistance that may be requested includes, but is not limited to, participating in HubSpot’s fact finding investigations, administrative proceedings, depositions, hearings, trial preparation, trial, other court or administrative proceedings and related activities. HubSpot shall pay you at a fixed rate of $1,500 per hour for all time reasonably spent providing cooperation or assistance under this Section excluding any time testifying under oath, including reasonable preparation and travel time, and shall reimburse you for all reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with such cooperation or assistance. Such payments and reimbursements shall be in addition to, and shall not reduce, the Severance Benefits and shall be made within thirty (30) days after your submission of an itemized invoice and reasonable supporting documentation. Any compensation for cooperation shall be solely for your time and services and shall not be contingent on the substance of your testimony or the outcome of any matter, and shall be payable only to the extent permitted by applicable law. The Indemnification Agreement by and between HubSpot and you, dated as of January 8, 2020, remains in full force and effect. 10 . Amendment. The Parties may modify this Agreement only in writing signed by the duly authorized representatives of both Parties. This Agreement is binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective agents, assigns, heirs, executors, successors and administrators. 11 . Waiver of Rights . No delay or omission by HubSpot in exercising any right under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver of that or any other right. A waiver or consent given by HubSpot on any one occasion shall be effective only in that instance and shall not be construed as a bar or waiver of any right on any other occasion. 7 12 . Validity. If any court of competent jurisdiction declares or determines any provision of this Agreement to be illegal or invalid, then the validity of the remaining parts, terms or provisions will not be affected, and the illegal or invalid provision will be deemed not to be a part of this Agreement. 13 . Nature of Agreement . You understand and agree that this Agreement is a separation agreement and does not constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing on the part of HubSpot. 14 . Acknowledgements . You affirm that no person or entity has offered or made any other promises or agreements of any kind to cause you to sign this Agreement, and that you fully understand the meaning and intent of this Agreement. You further affirm that you have carefully read this Agreement, understand its contents, freely and voluntarily assent to all of its terms and conditions and sign your name of your own free will. 15 . Applicable Law; Venue . This Agreement shall be interpreted and construed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to conflict of law provisions. You and HubSpot agree that any suit, action or other proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement or its subject matter must be brought in the state or federal courts in the State of California (which courts, for purposes of this Agreement, are the only courts of competent jurisdiction), and you and HubSpot irrevocably submit to and acknowledge the jurisdiction of these courts. 16 . Entire Agreement . Except for the agreements and affirmations referenced herein as surviving (which shall remain in full force and effect), this Agreement constitutes the entire understanding and agreement between you and HubSpot with respect to your separation from HubSpot and cancels all previous oral and written negotiations, agreements, commitments or writings in connection with the subject matter of this Agreement. 17 . Counterparts & Electronic Signature . This Agreement must be executed electronically via DocuSign unless otherwise required by law, and in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original and all of which together shall be deemed to be one and the same instrument. Each Party’s electronic signature on this Agreement shall have the same validity and force and effect as an original, wet signature. 8 If you choose to execute this Agreement, please return all pages of the Agreement via DocuSign, within the twenty-one (21) days described in Section 4(d). If you have any questions about the matters covered in this Agreement, please feel free to contact Helen Russell. 18. Code Section 409A . The parties intend that all payments and benefits provided under this Agreement either comply with, or be exempt from Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. To the extent applicable, the provisions of Section 10 of the Executive Severance Plan relating to Section 409A are incorporated herein by reference and shall govern the interpretation and administration of this Agreement. HubSpot, Inc. By: /s/ Helen Russell November 12, 2026 Name: Helen Russell Date Title: Chief People Officer You are advised to consult with an attorney before signing this Agreement. This is a legal document. Your signature will commit you to its terms. By signing below, you acknowledge that you have carefully read and fully understand all of the provisions of this Agreement and that you are knowingly and voluntarily entering into this Agreement. /s/ Yamini Rangan November 12, 2026 Yamini Rangan Date 9 Exhibit A CERTIFICATE UPDATING RELEASE OF CLAIMS I hereby acknowledge and certify that I entered into a letter agreement with HubSpot, Inc. (the “ Company ”), dated November 12, 2026 (the “ Agreement ”). Capitalized but undefined terms in this Certificate are defined in the Agreement. Pursuant to the Agreement, I am required to sign this “Certificate,” which updates the release of claims in the Agreement, in order to receive some of the severance benefits described in the Agreement. For this Certificate to become effective and for me to receive such severance benefits, I must sign this Certificate after the Separation Date but no later than twenty-one days after the Separation Date and must not revoke the Certificate. I understand that I may not sign this Certificate before the Separation Date. I further agree as follows: 1. A copy of this Certificate was attached as an Exhibit to the Agreement, and I have had at least 21 days to consider this Certificate. 2. In consideration of the benefits described in the Agreement, for which I become eligible only if I sign and do not revoke this Certificate, I hereby extend the release of claims set forth in the Agreement to any and all claims that arose after the date I signed the Agreement through the date I signed this Certificate, subject to all other exclusions and terms set forth in the Agreement. 3. I have carefully read and fully understand all of the provisions of this Certificate, I knowingly and voluntarily agree to all of the terms set forth in this Certificate, and I acknowledge that in entering into this Certificate, I am not relying on any representation, promise or inducement made by the Company or its officers, directors, employees, agents or other representatives with the exception of those promises expressly contained in this Certificate and the Agreement. 4. I understand I must sign this Certificate within twenty-one (21) days following the Separation Date. I further understand that I may revoke this Certificate within seven (7) days after I sign it by delivering a notice of revocation to the Company. If I do not sign the Certificate or if I revoke the Certificate, I will not be entitled to the severance payments and benefits set forth in the Agreement. This Certificate shall become effective the date following the conclusion of the revocation period (the “ Certificate Effective Date ”). 6. I agree that this Certificate is part of the Agreement. Accepted and Agreed: Yamini Rangan Date 10

title: HUBSPOT INC
text: EX-10.2 3 d77303dex102.htm EX-10.2 EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 November 12, 2026 Kate Bueker [***] [***] Dear Kate, This Letter Agreement (“Agreement”) confirms our agreement regarding your planned retirement and transition from the role of Chief Financial Officer of HubSpot, Inc. (the “ Company ”) to a non-executive advisory role, and the terms that will apply during and after that transition. You currently serve as the Company’s Chief Financial Officer pursuant to your offer letter with the Company dated May 14, 2018 (the “ Offer Letter ”). You are also party to the Company’s Executive Severance Plan as a Tier 2 Executive pursuant to a participation letter dated April 16, 2025 (together with the Executive Severance Plan attached thereto as Exhibit A, the “ Severance Plan ”). 1. Transition From Chief Financial Officer Role Effective as of February 11, 2027 (the “ Transition Date ”), you will step down from the position of Chief Financial Officer of the Company and from any other officer or similar positions you hold with the Company and its subsidiaries and affiliates, and you will cease to be an “executive officer” of the Company for purposes of applicable securities laws and the Company’s governance policies. Effective as of the Transition Date, you will transition to the non-executive role of advisor to the Company (the “ Advisor Role ”), reporting to the Chief Executive Officer or such other person as the Company may designate. Your at-will employment with the Company will continue through the Transition Date and until December 31, 2027 (the “ Separation Date ”). During the period beginning on the Transition Date and ending on the Separation Date (the “ Advisor Period ”), you will provide such transition, advisory, and other support services to the Company as the Chief Executive Officer may reasonably request from time to time, consistent with the non-executive, advisory nature of the Advisor Role. Prior to the Transition Date, you will continue to be covered under the Company’s existing directors and officers liability insurance policy (the “ D&O Policy ”) on the same basis as immediately prior to the date of this Agreement, consistent with your role as an executive officer of the Company. Effective as of the Transition Date, the Company will add you as an individually named insured under the D&O Policy, and will maintain such individual coverage for you through the Separation Date, in each case subject to the terms, conditions, and exclusions of the D&O Policy as in effect from time to time. 2. Compensation and Benefits You shall continue to receive all current pay, benefits and equity vesting applicable to your Chief Financial Officer role through the Transition Date. During the Advisor Period, the Company will also continue to pay your base salary at the rate, and in accordance with the same payroll practices, as in effect immediately prior to the Transition Date. You will receive your bonus payment for H2 2026 in the normal course, with payment on the company-wide payout date. You are not eligible for a 2027 bonus payment. 1 In addition, your outstanding equity awards will remain outstanding and will continue to vest in accordance with their existing vesting schedules throughout the Advisor Period, and, except as provided herein, subject to the terms of the applicable award agreements and the equity plans under which such awards were granted. Service in the Advisor Role will be treated as continued service for purposes of vesting of your outstanding equity awards. During the Advisor Period, you will remain eligible to participate in the Company’s employee benefit plans on the same basis as immediately prior to the Transition Date, subject to the terms of those plans as in effect from time to time and any changes applicable to similarly situated employees generally. You acknowledge and agree that, effective as of the Transition Date, you will cease to be a “Covered Executive” or “Tier 2 Executive” under, and will no longer participate in or be eligible for any payments or benefits under, the Severance Plan, including upon any termination of your employment with the Company on or after the Transition Date, whether in connection with a Change in Control or otherwise. Your participation in the Severance Plan will terminate in its entirety as of the Transition Date, and, except as provided below, the Severance Plan will have no further application to you from and after that date. For the avoidance of doubt, any notice you are required to provide regarding your planned retirement and transition shall not constitute a voluntary resignation without Good Reason for purposes of this Agreement or any other agreement with the Company. 3. At-Will Employment/Termination Prior to Separation Date Nothing in this Agreement changes the at-will nature of your employment with the Company. Either the Company or you may terminate your employment at any time prior to the Separation Date, with or without Cause or notice, subject to applicable law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if your employment and/or service is terminated prior to the Separation Date for any reason other than a termination by the Company for “Cause” (as defined in the Severance Plan) or by you due to voluntary resignation without Good Reason (as defined in the Severance Plan excluding subpart (iii)), then: (i) the unvested portion of each equity award outstanding immediately prior to such termination that would have vested on or before December 31, 2027 had you remained continuously employed through that date will immediately vest and, as applicable, become exercisable or nonforfeitable as of the later of (a) the Separation Date or (b) the effective date of the Separation Agreement and Release (as defined below); and (ii) the Company will pay you, in a single lump sum (less taxes and withholdings) within 30 days following the effective date of the Separation Agreement and Release (as defined below), an amount equal to the aggregate base salary you would have received for the period beginning on the day immediately following such termination and ending on December 31, 2027, calculated using the base salary rate applicable under this Agreement during the Advisor Period. The Company’s obligation to provide you with the acceleration and payments under this Section 3 shall be conditioned upon (i) your execution of a separation agreement and release in a form and manner satisfactory to and provided by the Company that contains a general release of claims in favor of the Company and related persons and entities (with standard exceptions), confidentiality, return of property and non-disparagement provisions, and a reaffirmation of the Continuing Obligations (the “ Separation Agreement and Release ”) and (ii) the Separation Agreement and Release becoming irrevocable, all within 60 days after the date of termination (or such shorter period set forth in the Separation Agreement and Release). 2 4. Continuing Obligations You hereby acknowledge the Employee Invention, Non-Disclosure, Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation Agreement dated as of June 18, 2018 (the “ Restrictive Covenant Agreement ”), that was attached to your Offer Letter. The Company hereby waives, and will not seek to enforce, the non-competition covenant set forth in Paragraph (b) under the heading “Non-Compete/Non-Solicitation” in the Restrictive Covenant Agreement. Except for the non-competition covenant, you hereby agree, effective as of the date you sign this Agreement, to be bound by all of the remaining terms of the Restrictive Covenant Agreement, including the provisions relating to inventions and patents, proprietary information, non-solicitation of employees, independent contractors, and customers, and the other obligations, representations, and miscellaneous provisions set forth in the Restrictive Covenant Agreement (together, the “ Continuing Obligations ”), each of which is incorporated into this Agreement by reference as if fully set forth herein, and by signing this Agreement, you hereby execute and agree to be bound by the Continuing Obligations. 5. Miscellaneous The payments and benefits provided under this Agreement are intended to be exempt from, or comply with, Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (“ Section 409A ”), and this Agreement will be interpreted accordingly. To the extent any payment or benefit constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation subject to Section 409A and is payable upon termination of employment, it will be payable only upon a “separation from service” within the meaning of Section 409A. If you are a “specified employee” within the meaning of Section 409A at such separation from service, any payment or benefit required to be delayed under Section 409A will be paid or provided on the earlier of the date that is six months and one day after your separation from service or your death. Acceleration of vesting under this Agreement will not accelerate settlement of an award subject to Section 409A except as permitted by Section 409A; any such award will be settled on its otherwise applicable payment date. This Agreement, together with the Restrictive Covenant Agreement and June 2018 Indemnification Agreement, and the other documents referenced herein (including but not limited to your equity award agreements), constitutes the entire agreement between you and the Company with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings, oral or written, with respect to such subject matter. This Agreement may not be amended or modified except by a written instrument signed by both you and the Company. This Agreement will be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions will continue in full force and effect. Kate, we are grateful for your leadership as Chief Financial Officer and look forward to your continued contributions in the Advisor Role. To confirm your agreement to the terms set forth in this Agreement, please sign below and return a copy to me. 3 Sincerely, HUBSPOT, INC. By: /s/ Helen Russell Name: Helen Russell Title: Chief People Officer I agree to the terms set forth in this Agreement. /s/ Kate Bueker Kate Bueker Date: November 12, 2026 4

title: Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance Liquidating Trust
text: EX-10.2 3 d896886dex102.htm EX-10.2 EX-10.2 Exhibit 10.2 ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION AGREEMENT THIS ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION AGREEMENT, by and between Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance, Inc., a Maryland corporation (“Assignor”), and Apollo Commercial Real Estate Finance Liquidating Trust, a Maryland statutory trust (the “Trust”), is entered into as of November 6, 2026 (this “Agreement”). W I T N E S S E T H : WHEREAS, reference is hereby made to that certain Plan of Complete Liquidation and Dissolution of Assignor, adopted by the stockholders of Assignor on September 29, 2026 (the “Plan”), which provides that Assignor may transfer and assign to the Trust any assets of Assignor as the Board of Directors of Assignor shall determine, including its unsold properties, loans, securities, interests in subsidiaries of Assignor, cash, reserves, assets, claims, contingent claims, causes of action, rights, privileges, books and records, and attorney-client privilege and work product, subject to all of their unsatisfied debts, claims, obligations, liabilities and expenses, contingent or otherwise, and the Trust shall assume, pay, satisfy, discharge or perform when due all such unsatisfied debts, claims, obligations, liabilities and expenses, as well as any and all other debts, claims, obligations, liabilities and expenses of Assignor, whether contingent or otherwise; WHEREAS, as contemplated by the Plan, Assignor desires to transfer, convey, assign and deliver all of its assets, including its unsold properties, loans, securities, interests in subsidiaries of Assignor, cash, reserves, assets, claims, contingent claims, causes of action, rights, privileges, books and records, attorney-client privilege and work product, excluding only those assets set forth on Schedule A hereto (the assets set forth on Schedule A, collectively, the “Excluded Assets” and, the assets of Assignor other than the Excluded Assets, collectively, the “Assigned Assets”), to the Trust (such transfer, the “Asset Transfer”), and the Trust desires to accept such Assigned Assets, subject to all debts, claims, obligations, liabilities and expenses of Assignor, contingent or otherwise, and to assume, pay, satisfy, discharge or perform when due all debts, claims, obligations, guarantees, liabilities and expenses of Assignor of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, fixed, contingent, conditional, unliquidated, unmatured, disputed or undisputed, asserted before or after the Effective Time (as defined below), arising in contract, by statute, in tort, by judicial or administrative action or otherwise, and payable or performable before or after the Effective Time, and whether or not set forth on any schedule or associated with any particular Assigned Asset (collectively, the “Assumed Liabilities”); and WHEREAS, the Trust further desires to defend, indemnify, reimburse and hold harmless Assignor from and against any known or unknown, contingent or unmatured claim and any expenses or obligations of Assignor that may arise or become known after the date hereof, as more fully set forth in Section 2 hereof. NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration to Assignor, receipt of which is hereby acknowledged, Assignor and the Trust, intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows: 1. Assumption of Liabilities; Successor Obligations . Effective as of 2:00 p.m., Eastern Time, on November 9, 2026 (the “Effective Time”), the Trust hereby expressly assumes all of the Assumed Liabilities, and agrees to pay, satisfy, discharge or perform them when due. Pursuant to Section 3-115(c) of the Maryland General Corporation Law (the “MGCL”), the Trust, as successor to Assignor, is liable for all debts and obligations of Assignor, including the Assumed Liabilities (the obligations of the Trust as such successor under Section 3-115(c) of the MGCL, together with its obligations under this Section 1, the “Successor Obligations”), which obligations are absolute, unconditional, continuing and cumulative, are not subject to any cap, and are not limited to any scheduled obligations or to liabilities associated with any particular Assigned Assets; provided, however, that the Trust shall succeed to and have the benefit of all rights, defenses, counterclaims, setoffs, recoupments, limitations and other objections that the Assignor had or would have had with respect to any such debt or obligation, and no creditor of the Assignor shall have any greater right, claim or remedy against the Trust than such creditor had or would have had against the Assignor. The Asset Transfer is intended to be a “transfer of assets” for purposes of the MGCL, including Sections 1-101 and 3-115 thereof, and this Agreement is the agreement contemplated by Section 3-115 of the MGCL and is intended to extend the liability of the Trust to the full scope of the Assumed Liabilities. The Trust is a primary obligor, and not a guarantor or secondary obligor, with respect to all Assumed Liabilities. Nothing in this Agreement, the Asset Transfer, the dissolution of Assignor or the assumption of the Assumed Liabilities shall release, extinguish, compromise or impair any right or remedy of any creditor of Assignor; such assumption is not a novation; and no creditor shall be required first to proceed against Assignor or any other person. 2. Assignor Indemnity . From and after the Effective Time, the Trust shall defend, indemnify, reimburse and hold harmless Assignor from and against any and all liabilities, judgments, settlements, costs, obligations, losses, damages, charges and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees, litigation expenses, enforcement costs and settlement amounts) that (a) arise out of, result from, relate to or are incurred in connection with any Assumed Liability or (b) are incurred by Assignor after the Effective Time (collectively, the “Assignor Indemnity”). The Assignor Indemnity is a present, direct and enforceable obligation of the Trust; applies to matters known or unknown and asserted before or after the dissolution of Assignor; covers third-party claims and direct losses, including costs of defense and of enforcing this Section 2; is separate from and cumulative of the assumption of the Assumed Liabilities and the Successor Obligations; and shall survive the Asset Transfer, the dissolution of Assignor, the termination of this Agreement and the termination of the Trust for so long as any matter covered hereby remains outstanding. The Assignor Indemnity shall not be subject to any procedural condition that would materially narrow or delay its protection, and any failure or delay by Assignor or any other person in giving notice of any matter shall not relieve the Trust of any obligation hereunder. 3. Assignment of Assets . As of the Effective Time, Assignor hereby transfers, conveys, assigns and delivers to the Trust, its successors and assigns, to have and to hold forever, all of Assignor’s right, title and interest in, to and under the Assigned Assets, and the Trust hereby accepts and assumes all of the Assigned Assets. Assignor hereby covenants and agrees that it will, at the reasonable request of the Trust, and without further consideration, execute and deliver such other instruments of transfer, conveyance and assignment, and take such other action, if any, as may reasonably be necessary to effect, consummate, confirm or evidence the transfer to the Trust, its successors and assigns valid title to the Assigned Assets. 4. Issuance of Units . In exchange for the assumption of the Assumed Liabilities and the Asset Transfer, as of the Effective Time, the Trust hereby agrees to issue 130,113,515 units of beneficial interest, par value $0.01 per unit (the “Units”), of the Trust to Assignor. The issuance of Units shall be exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and applicable state and local laws requiring registration of securities. 5. Power of Attorney . Assignor hereby constitutes and appoints the Trust (or its successors and assigns) the true and lawful attorney and attorneys of Assignor, with full power of substitution, in the name of the Trust or in the name and stead of Assignor, but on behalf of, for the benefit and at the expense of the Trust, its successors and assigns: (a) to collect, demand and receive any and all Assigned Assets hereby assigned to the Trust and to give receipts and releases for and in respect of the same; and (b) to institute and prosecute any and all actions, suits or proceedings, at law, in equity or otherwise, which the Trust may deem proper in order to collect, assert or enforce any claim, right or title of any kind in or to the Assigned Assets hereby assigned to the Trust, to defend or compromise any and all actions, suits or proceedings in respect of any of the Assigned Assets, and to do all such acts and things in relation thereto as the Trust shall deem advisable. Assignor acknowledges that the foregoing powers are coupled with an interest and shall be irrevocable by it or upon its subsequent dissolution or in any manner or for any reason. The Trust shall be entitled to retain for its own account any amounts collected pursuant to the foregoing powers, including any amounts payable as interest with respect thereto. 6. No Representations . The parties acknowledge and agree that the Assigned Assets are being transferred on an “as is” basis without any representations or warranties with respect thereto. 7. Third Party Beneficiaries . Each creditor of Assignor and each creditor of ACREFI Mortgage Lending, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“ACREFI”), in each case to the extent its claim, right, debt, obligation or liability is encompassed by the Assumed Liabilities, the Successor Obligations, the Assignor Indemnity or another covered obligation of the Trust hereunder, including known or unknown, fixed or contingent, matured or unmatured and liquidated or unliquidated creditors and claimants (collectively, the “Creditor Beneficiaries”), is an intended, and not an incidental, third-party beneficiary of Sections 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12 hereof and of each other covenant herein relating to the assumption of the Assumed Liabilities, the Successor Obligations, the Assignor Indemnity or the preservation of creditor rights. Each Creditor Beneficiary may enforce such provisions directly against the Trust in its own name, without any requirement of reliance, privity or exhaustion of remedies against Assignor or any other person, and may seek damages, specific performance, injunctive relief and any other relief available at law or in equity. This Section 7 does not by itself constitute an independent assumption by the Trust of any liability of ACREFI that is not otherwise covered by this Agreement, but affords full direct enforcement rights to the extent such liability is so covered. Except as provided in this Section 7, nothing herein, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person any legal or equitable right, benefit or remedy of any nature whatsoever, under or by reason of this Agreement. 8. Specific Performance . The parties agree that irreparable damage would occur in the event that any of the provisions of this Agreement were not performed in accordance with their specific terms or were otherwise breached. It is accordingly agreed that, notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, the parties and, with respect to the obligations of the Trust enforceable by them under Section 7 hereof, the Creditor Beneficiaries are entitled, in addition to any other remedy to which they are or may be entitled at law or in equity, to seek an injunction or injunctions to prevent breaches of this Agreement and to enforce specifically the terms and provisions hereof. The foregoing rights are in addition to and without limitation of any other remedy to which the parties or the Creditor Beneficiaries may be entitled at law or in equity. The parties further agree not to assert that a remedy of specific performance is unenforceable, invalid, contrary to law or inequitable for any reason, nor to assert that a remedy of monetary damages would provide an adequate remedy. Each of the parties hereby waives (a) any defenses in any actions, suits or proceedings for specific performance, including the defense that a remedy at law would be adequate and (b) any requirement under any applicable law to post a bond or other security as a prerequisite to obtaining equitable relief. 9. Assignment . This Agreement may not be assigned by operation of law or otherwise without the express written consent of the Trust. No assignment by the Trust of this Agreement or of any of its rights or obligations hereunder shall release the Trust from any of its obligations hereunder, including the Successor Obligations and the Assignor Indemnity, and no assignment shall be made in contravention of Section 10 hereof. 10. Amendment, Waiver and Termination; Creditor Protection . Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, no amendment, waiver, release, assignment, termination or other modification of this Agreement, and no distribution of assets of the Trust (which shall be made only in accordance with Section 4.2 of the Declaration of Trust (as defined below)), may materially and adversely impair the rights of any Creditor Beneficiary hereunder unless the claim of such Creditor Beneficiary has first been paid, satisfied, discharged or adequately provided for. 11. Limitation of Recourse . Recourse for the obligations of the Trust hereunder shall be solely to the Trust and its assets, and no trustee, officer or holder of Units, nor the Manager (as defined in the Declaration of Trust), shall have any personal liability for any such obligation. Nothing in this Section shall limit the recourse of Assignor or any Creditor Beneficiary to the Trust and all of the Trust Assets (as defined in the Declaration of Trust). 12. Relationship to Declaration of Trust . The obligations of the Trust hereunder and under the Amended and Restated Agreement and Declaration of Trust of the Trust, dated as of November 6, 2026 (as amended from time to time, the “Declaration of Trust”), are cumulative, and neither this Agreement nor the Declaration of Trust shall be construed to narrow or limit the other. 13. Governing Law . This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Maryland applicable to contracts executed in and to be performed in that state and without regard to any applicable conflicts of law. 14. Binding Nature . This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and assigns, including any successor to the Trust by merger, consolidation, conversion or transfer of assets. 15. Counterparts . This Agreement may be executed in several counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all such counterparts shall constitute one and the same instrument. [Signature Page Follows] IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed as of the date first written above by their respective officers or trustees thereunto duly authorized.
