FOR VALUE RECEIVED, M2i Global, Inc., a Nevada corporation with an address at 885 Tahoe Boulevard, Incline Village, NV, 89451, United States of America (hereinafter referred to as the “ Maker ”), promises to pay to the order of Happy Growth Group Limited, a British Virgin Islands company (hereinafter referred to as “ Payee ”) having an address at 11 th Floor, COFCO Tower, 262 Gloucester Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, or at such other place as may be designated in writing by the holder of this promissory note (this “ Note ”), the principal sum of $3,000,000 (Three Million United States Dollars), with all principal due and payable in full in the earlier to occur of (x) December 31, 2026 or as mutually agreed between Maker and Payee or (y) an Event of Default (as defined in Section 6 hereof). 2. Guaranty by GTL . All obligations of the Maker under this Note, including without limitation, payment of principal, shall be unconditionally guaranteed by Graphex Technologies LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“ GTL ”), and the holder of this Note shall be entitled to all of the benefits of such guarantee. The Guaranty attached hereto as Exhibit A and executed as of even date with this Note is hereby incorporated by reference. 3. Prepayment . Maker may at any time voluntarily prepay this Note in full or in part, without premium or penalty. 4. Covenants . For so long as all or any portion of the principal under this Note outstanding, the Maker shall not take any of the following actions with respect to GTL, and shall cause GTL to not take any of the following actions, in each case, without the prior written consent of the Payee: (a) sell, assign, transfer, redeem, pledge or otherwise dispose of or encumber any of the limited liability company interests of GTL; - 1 - (b) permit GTL to issue any additional limited liability company interest or other equity interest, or any option, warrant or other right to acquire an equity interest; (c) cause the GTL to fail to maintain its existence and good standing under Delaware law; (d) not promptly notify the Payee of any change in the legal name, trade name, jurisdiction or form of organization, or organizational identification number of GTL; or (e) take any action that would cause a material breach or default under the terms and conditions of the amended and restated limited liability company agreement of GTL. 5. Event of Default . At the option of the holder, this Note and all principal payable hereby shall become immediately due and payable (“ Event of Default ”) with written notice or demand upon: (a) the occurrence at any time of a default in any payment of principal or interest due hereunder, which default is not cured within ten (10) business days after the date such payment was due; (b) in the event that Maker shall, at any time prior to the payment of the entire amount of principal, fail to own, beneficially and of record, one hundred percent (100%) of the limited liability company interests or other equity interests in GTL or any surviving, resulting or successor entity; or (c) If the Maker or GTL shall make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or shall commence a case under the federal bankruptcy laws, or any state insolvency laws, or shall file any petition or answer seeking for itself any reorganization, arrangement, composition, readjustment, liquidation, dissolution or similar relief under any present or future statute, law or regulation, or shall file an answer admitting or not contesting the material allegations of a petition against it in any such proceeding, or shall seek or acquiesce in the appointment of any trustee, custodian, receiver or liquidator of any such entity; or if, within 60 days after the commencement of an action against any such entity seeking any reorganization, arrangement, composition, readjustment, liquidation, dissolution or similar relief under any present or future statute, such action shall not have been dismissed or all orders entered therein or proceedings thereunder affecting its business, operations and properties shall not have been vacated, or any such entity shall otherwise liquidate its business or cease operating as a going concern. 6. Rights and Remedies After An Event of Default. Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, simple interest at the rate of two percent (2%) per annum, from the date of occurrence of an Event of Default until the full payment or settlement of the principal shall be payable by the Maker to the Payee. Interest on the principal shall be computed on the basis of the actual number of days the principal is outstanding on the basis of a 365-day or 366-day year, as is applicable. Interest shall accrue on the principal on the day on which s an Event of Default occurs, and shall not accrue on the day on which, the principal or any portion of the principal, is paid. Further, the Payee may, without prior notice or demand to the Maker (except as required by applicable law that cannot be waived), in addition to all rights and remedies available under the Note, the UCC and other applicable law: (a) exercise all voting, management, economic and other rights relating to the Pledged Interests and receive all distributions thereon; - 2 - (b) collect, receive, hold, sell, assign or otherwise dispose of any or all Pledged Interests at public or private sale, in one or more transactions, on commercially reasonable terms; and (c) exercise any other right or remedy of a secured party with respect to the Pledged Interests. 7. Proxy and Power of Attorney . The Maker grants to the Payee an irrevocable proxy, coupled with an interest, effective only upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, to (a) receive and endorse distributions, (b) make necessary filings, and (c) and take other actions reasonably necessary to enforce this Agreement. The Payee shall have no obligation to exercise any such power. 8. Application of Proceeds . The Payee shall apply cash and proceeds received through enforcement first to the reasonable costs and expenses of enforcement, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, and then to the principal followed, subject to applicable law. The Maker remains liable for any deficiency, and any surplus shall be paid to the Maker or other person legally entitled thereto. 9. Payment of Expenses . In addition to and not in limitation of the foregoing, Maker further agrees to pay all expenses, including reasonable attorney’s fees and legal expenses, incurred by the holder of this Note in collecting or attempting to collect any amounts payable hereunder which are not paid when due, whether by acceleration or otherwise. The Maker for itself and its successors and assigns hereby waive the right to trial by jury in any action or proceeding instituted in respect of this Note. 10. Waiver and Amendments . No delay or omission on the part of the holder in exercising any right hereunder shall operate as a waiver of such right or of any other right of such holder, nor shall any delay, omission or waiver on any one occasion be deemed a bar to or waiver of the same or any other right on any future occasion. No term of this Note may be waived, modified, or amended except by an instrument in writing signed by both the Maker and the Payee. 11. Successors and Assigns . This Note shall be binding upon the Maker, GTL and their respective successors and permitted assigns and shall inure to the benefit of the Payee and its successors and assigns. The Payee may, at any time and without notice to or the consent of the Maker, assign, transfer or sell this Note in whole, but not in part, or pledge this Note or any of its rights hereunder. Any successor or assignee of the Payee shall succeed to the rights so assigned or transferred and, to the extent thereof, shall be deemed the “Payee” for purposes of this Note. The Maker may not assign or delegate any of its rights or obligations under this Note without the prior written consent of the Payee not to be unreasonably withheld. 12. Governing law and Jurisdiction . This Note and all rights and obligations hereunder, including matters of construction, validity and performance, shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and performed entirely within the State of New York without regard to conflicts of law rules applied in the State of New York. The Maker for itself and its successors and assigns hereby consents to personal jurisdiction over it and them in the courts of the State of New York, county of New York and of any federal court located in such jurisdiction in connection with any action or proceeding arising out of or related to this Note. The Maker for itself and its successors and assigns agrees that service of process upon it or them may be made in any manner permitted by the laws of the State of New York and in addition thereto specifically agrees that service of process will be deemed sufficient for personal jurisdiction over it or them if service is made by registered or certified mail, to Maker’s address as set forth herein or to any office or successor office established by Maker or such party. 13. Severability . Any provision hereof which may prove invalid, illegal, or unenforceable under any law shall not affect the validity of any other provision hereof. 14. This Note may not be terminated orally, but only by a writing signed by the holder thereof. 15. Termination and Release. After the obligations have been indefeasibly paid and performed in full and the Payee has no further commitment or contingent claim under the Note, the Payee shall, at the Maker’s expense, release its security interest, return any certificates and transfer instruments held by it, and authorize the filing of appropriate UCC termination statements. text: EX-10.1 2 ea031209301ex10-1.htm EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT DATED NOVEMBER 9, 2026, BY AND BETWEEN THE COMPANY AND CHAN PHANG CHUEN Exhibit 10.1 Chief Technical Officer Executive Employment Agreement This Chief Technical Officer Executive Employment Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into by and between the following parties on the basis of equality, voluntariness and consensus: Party A (the “Company”): Next Technology Holding Inc. (NASDAQ: NXTT), a company incorporated under the laws of the State of Wyoming, USA. Party B (the “Executive”): Full Name: CHAN PHANG CHUEN; Valid ID Number: A71111770. WHEREAS the Company, pursuing its dual-engine strategy of “AI plus digital assets,” intends to appoint the Executive as its Chief Technical Officer to assume overall responsibility for its technology strategy, research and development, and engineering organization; and WHEREAS the Executive accepts such appointment; NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows: Article 1 Position, Duties and Reporting 1.1 Position: The Company appoints the Executive as Chief Technical Officer (CTO), a senior executive officer of the Company. The Executive shall report to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and the Board of Directors (the “Board”). 1.2 Overall duties: The Executive shall devote full business time, attention and best efforts to the Company, act with the highest duty of care and loyalty, and assume overall responsibility for the following matters: (1) Technology strategy: formulate and execute the Company’s overall technology strategy and technology roadmap in alignment with the dual-engine strategy, and lead the technology planning across AI-integrated SaaS, AI computing, and robotics and embodied intelligence; (2) Research and development: oversee the technical execution of the Company’s R&D program, including the approved R&D budget of US$35 million, and be accountable for the allocation of R&D resources, milestone delivery and technology reserves; (3) Engineering organization: lead, recruit, develop and evaluate the entire technology organization, and build its organizational structure, talent pipeline and engineering standards; (4) Architecture and operations: be responsible for enterprise-level technical architecture, information security, data governance, MLOps platforms, system availability and disaster recovery; 1 / 9 (5) Corporate governance: report regularly to the CEO and the Board, participate in major corporate decisions and technology due diligence, and support internal control over financial reporting and the technical matters relevant to the Company’s SEC disclosures; (6) Intellectual property: direct the intellectual property strategy, patent portfolio and technical compliance; and (7) External representation: serve as the senior technical representative before key customers, partners, regulators and industry bodies, and perform other duties lawfully assigned by the CEO and the Board. 1.3 The Executive shall comply with the Company’s articles, bylaws, policies and lawful resolutions, and shall not hold any other employment, office or conflicting business engagement without the Board’s prior written consent. Article 2 Term 2.1 This Agreement is valid for one (1) year, from November 9, 2026 to November 8, 2027. The parties may negotiate to renew it upon expiration. Any continuation of service after expiration shall be subject to the Company’s policies and any written renewal. Article 3 Base Salary 3.1 Monthly base salary: The Executive’s monthly base salary is USD 40,000, corresponding to an annual base salary of USD 480,000 . 3.2 Payment: The base salary shall be paid in cash by wire transfer to the bank account designated by the Executive before the 25th day of each month. The Company may review and adjust the salary in accordance with its compensation policies. 3.3 Taxes: The Executive shall bear the individual income taxes and other levies lawfully payable, and the Company may withhold such taxes where required by law. Article 4 Annual Performance Bonus 4.1 Target bonus: The Executive shall be eligible for an annual performance bonus with a target amount equal to fifty percent (50%) of the annual base salary (the target being USD 240,000), determined based on the achievement of Company and individual performance objectives. 2 / 9 4.2 Payout factor: The actual bonus may range from zero percent (0%) to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the target amount, as certified by the Board or the compensation committee, and shall be paid following the relevant performance period. 4.3 Share-based payment: The Company may, at its discretion, pay all or part of the bonus in cash, in shares of common stock or restricted stock units, or in a combination thereof. Any equity portion shall be valued by reference to the closing price of the common stock on the relevant grant or payment date, and the number of shares shall be calculated accordingly. 4.4 The bonus is not guaranteed unless otherwise expressly agreed in writing, and the Executive must remain employed on the payment date to be eligible, except as otherwise provided in Article 13. Article 5 Special R&D Incentive Award 5.1 Subject to the successful progress of the Company’s research and development results, the Company may, upon approval by the Board or the compensation committee, grant the Executive a personal incentive award of up to USD 10,000,000 in each year. 5.2 The award may be paid in cash and/or in shares of common stock (including restricted stock units). Any share portion shall be valued by reference to the closing price of the common stock on the relevant grant or payment date, and the number of shares shall be calculated accordingly. 5.3 The award is discretionary and not guaranteed. Its grant, amount and payment are subject to Board approval and the availability of funds; where equity is used, it shall comply with the applicable rules of the 2025 Plan and shall be subject to the Clawback Policy. Article 6 Equity Incentive Awards 6.1 The Executive shall be eligible for equity awards under the Next Technology Holding Inc. 2025 Equity Incentive Plan (the “2025 Plan”), the securities under which are registered by the Company on Form S-8. 6.2 Initial award: Upon commencement, the Executive shall receive an initial service-based equity award; the number of shares, grant price and vesting schedule shall be specified in a separate grant agreement, with the grant-date fair value determined by the closing price of the common stock on the grant date. 3 / 9 6.3 Annual and performance awards: The Executive may receive annual equity awards and performance-based restricted stock units tied to the achievement of R&D milestones, AI product commercialization and team-building objectives, as determined by the Board or the compensation committee. 6.4 Clawback: All awards are subject to the 2025 Plan and the Company’s Clawback Policy, and may be recovered in the event of a financial restatement or the Executive’s misconduct. 6.5 Upon termination, the treatment of vested and unvested awards shall follow the 2025 Plan and the applicable grant agreements; unvested awards shall generally be forfeited. Article 7 Benefits, Insurance and Reimbursement 7.1 The Executive shall be entitled to the employee benefits and insurance programs made available by the Company to its senior executives, in accordance with the applicable policies. 7.2 The Company shall reimburse the Executive for reasonable and documented business expenses incurred in the performance of duties, upon approval in accordance with its policies. Article 8 Confidentiality 8.1 During the term and for two (2) years after termination, the Executive shall keep confidential, and shall not disclose or use without permission, the Company’s trade secrets and confidential information, including technical architectures, source code, models, algorithms, data, R&D plans and budgets, business strategies, customer resources and pricing. 8.2 The confidentiality obligations with respect to trade secrets not lawfully made public shall continue until such information becomes public. Article 9 Intellectual Property 9.1 Present assignment: The Executive hereby irrevocably assigns to the Company, to the fullest extent permitted by law, all right, title and interest in all work product created within the scope of employment or using the Company’s resources, including inventions, software, source code, models, algorithms, designs, documents and all related intellectual property rights. 9.2 The Executive shall promptly disclose such work product, execute the necessary assignment and application documents, and assist the Company in protecting and enforcing its rights. 9.3 Intellectual property lawfully owned by the Executive before employment shall remain vested in the Executive; to the extent embedded in the work product, the Executive shall grant the Company a license necessary for its use. 4 / 9 Article 10 Non-Competition, Non-Solicitation and Non-Poaching 10.1 During the term, the Executive shall not engage in any business competing with the Company, nor hold any interest in any competing entity, except for passive holdings of publicly traded securities below the applicable thresholds. 10.2 For twelve (12) months after termination, the Executive shall not, within the markets where the Company operates, engage in any competing business concerning AI-enabled SaaS, AI computing, agentic commerce, digital assets or robotics, whether as an employee, officer, consultant, investor or otherwise. 10.3 During the same period, the Executive shall not solicit or induce the Company’s employees to leave, nor solicit the Company’s customers or partners for competing business. 10.4 These restrictions are intended to be reasonable and enforceable to the maximum extent permitted by law; any provision held unenforceable shall be limited or severed to the extent necessary. Article 11 Conflicts of Interest and Ethics 11.1 The Executive shall avoid any conflict between personal interests and those of the Company, shall not usurp corporate opportunities, and shall not accept undisclosed benefits from third parties in connection with the Company’s business. 11.2 The Executive shall comply with the Company’s code of conduct, insider trading policies, anti-corruption and anti-fraud requirements, and all applicable laws and regulations. Article 12 Anti-Fraud 12.1 The Executive shall not engage in, authorize, direct, conceal or facilitate any fraudulent, corrupt or dishonest act, including: (1) the falsification, misrepresentation or deliberate omission of the Company’s books, records, accounts, financial statements or SEC disclosures; (2) fraud, embezzlement, misappropriation or unauthorized use of the Company’s funds, assets (including digital assets such as Bitcoin), R&D budgets or other resources; (3) falsification of work product, R&D results, performance data or supporting documents; (4) bribery, kickbacks, or the offer or receipt of unlawful benefits; and (5) aiding, abetting or covering up any of the foregoing, or evading the Company’s internal controls. (6) The personal resume submitted to the company must be truthful and accurate. 5 / 9 12.2 The Executive shall maintain and comply with the Company’s internal controls, anti-fraud and anti-corruption policies and audit procedures, promptly report any suspected fraud through the appropriate channels, and cooperate with investigations; the Company shall not permit retaliation against any good-faith report. 12.3 Any breach of this Article constitutes Cause for immediate termination under Article 13. The Company may recover any bonus or equity award (including under the Clawback Policy), pursue damages and other available remedies, and the Executive shall not be indemnified for liabilities arising from fraud or willful misconduct. Article 13 Termination 13.1 Termination for Cause: The Company may terminate immediately for Cause, meaning: (1) conviction of, or charge involving, a felony or fraud or dishonesty; (2) material neglect of duties or refusal to follow lawful directions of the CEO or the Board; (3) intentional conduct materially harming the Company; (4) breach of confidentiality, intellectual property, non-competition or conflict-of-interest obligations; or (5) serious violation of Company policies. 13.2 Termination without Cause: The Company may terminate without Cause upon thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, or by paying thirty (30) days of base salary in lieu of notice. 13.3 Good Reason: The Executive may terminate for Good Reason upon: (1) a material reduction (in excess of ten percent (10%)) in base salary or target bonus; (2) a material demotion in title, duties or authority; (3) relocation of the principal workplace by more than fifty (50) kilometers; or (4) a successor failing to assume this Agreement, in each case without cure within thirty (30) days after written notice. 13.4 Resignation: The Executive shall give at least sixty (60) days’ prior written notice for a voluntary resignation. 13.5 Upon termination, the Executive shall complete the work handover, return Company property and documents, and continue to be bound by Articles 8, 9, 10 and 11 as applicable. Article 14 Liability for Breach 14.1 A party breaching this Agreement shall bear the corresponding liability and shall compensate the other party for the losses caused, subject to the limits and remedies expressly provided herein. 14.2 If the Executive’s breach of confidentiality or non-competition causes losses, the Company may seek injunctive relief in addition to damages and any other available remedies. 6 / 9 Article 15 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution 15.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Wyoming, USA. 15.2 Any dispute shall first be resolved through friendly negotiation; if negotiation fails, either party may bring a lawsuit before the court with jurisdiction at the Company’s registered address. Article 16 Miscellaneous 16.1 This Agreement is made in duplicate, one copy for each party, with the same legal effect. 16.2 The performance objectives attached hereto form an integral part of this Agreement. 16.3 Any amendment or supplement shall be made in writing and signed by both parties. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties concerning its subject matter. 16.4 This Agreement shall take effect after both parties sign or seal it. 7 / 9 [Signature Page] Party A: Next Technology Holding Inc. Authorized Representative (Signature): /s/ Weihong Liu Date: November 9, 2026 Party B (Signature): /s/ Chan Phang Chuen Date: November 9, 2026 8 / 9 Attachment: Performance Objectives and Assessment Framework Chief Technical Officer (CTO) 1. R&D Strategy and Execution: achievement rate of the milestones under the US$35 million R&D program; budget variance; and the accumulation of technology reserves such as core products and patents. The successful progress of these R&D results also serves as the condition for the Special R&D Incentive Award under Article 5. 2. Technical Operations: availability of core platforms (target no less than 99.9%); zero major information security or data incidents; and stable operation of MLOps and model release processes. 3. Business and Team: AI product commercialization and customer delivery; and the fill rate and retention of key technology positions. 4. Governance and Compliance: internal controls relevant to technology, cooperation with audits, and the filing of intellectual property applications. The specific indicators, targets and weighting for each dimension shall be set annually by the Board or the compensation committee and shall serve as the basis for the annual performance bonus, performance-based equity awards and the Special R&D Incentive Award. 9 / 9

text: EX-10.1 5 ex10_1.htm MENDMENT NO. 3 TO PROMISSORY NOTE STEWARDS INC. AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO PROMISSORY NOTE THIS AMENDMENT NO. 3 (this “Amendment”) to that certain Promissory Note dated June 1, 2023 in the original principal amount of US $4,700,000 (the “Original Note”), as amended by that certain Amendment No. 1 to Promissory Note dated as of June 1, 2026 (the “First Amendment”) and that certain Amendment No. 2 to Promissory Note dated as of September 1, 2026 (the “Second Amendment,” and together with the Original Note and the First Amendment, the “Note”), by and between Stewards Inc. , a Nevada corporation formerly known as Favo Capital, Inc. (the “Company” or “Maker”), and FAVO Holdings, LLC (the “Holder”), is entered into as of October 15, 2026 (the “Effective Date”). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings given in the Note. RECITALS A. Under the Note, the final installment of principal in the amount of $1,600,000 (the “Final Installment”), together with accrued interest at 6.0% per annum through May 31, 2026 and at 10.0% per annum thereafter pursuant to the First Amendment and the Second Amendment, was due and payable on October 15, 2026. Interest is computed on the basis of a 365-day or 366-day year, as applicable, and actual days elapsed, save as otherwise provided in the First Amendment, the Second Amendment and this Amendment. The Final Installment is held by the Holder, which is owned 65% by Vincent Napolitano and 35% by Shaun Quin. B. The Final Installment remains outstanding. The Company and the Holder desire to further extend its maturity to January 15, 2027, to continue the interest rate applicable from June 1, 2026, and to extend the waiver of the default interest rate so that no default interest applies with respect to any period up to and including January 15, 2027, as set out herein, in order to bring the obligation into compliance and provide for its orderly repayment. The parties intend this Amendment to take effect as of October 15, 2026 and to keep it a simple amendment of the Note. C. Section 11(d) of the Original Note provides that the Original Note may not be modified or amended except in a writing executed by the party to be charged, and Section 13 of the Original Note expressly authorizes renewals, extensions and modifications of the terms of payment thereunder. This Amendment constitutes such a writing and is executed by the Company and the Holder. AGREEMENT NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: 1. Amendment of Maturity. Section 2(a) of the Original Note, as amended by the First Amendment and the Second Amendment, is hereby further amended so that the Final Installment of principal in the amount of $1,600,000, previously due and payable on October 15, 2026, shall instead be due and payable in full on January 15, 2027 (the “Extended Maturity Date”). 2. Interest Rate. The outstanding principal of $1,600,000 shall continue to bear simple interest at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum, computed on a consistent straight-line basis per month, for the period from October 15, 2026 through January 15, 2027, aggregating Forty Thousand Dollars ($40,000.00), which shall be due and payable on the Extended Maturity Date together with the Final Installment and any other accrued and unpaid interest then outstanding. 3. Limited Waiver of Default Interest Rate. The fifteen percent (15%) per annum default interest rate set forth in Section 6(a) of the Original Note is hereby waived solely with respect to the period from June 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 (the “Extension Period”), including with respect to any failure to pay the Final Installment on May 31, 2026, September 1, 2026 or October 15, 2026. During the Extension Period, no default interest shall accrue, and the outstanding principal shall bear interest solely at the ten percent (10%) per annum rate set forth in Section 2 above. For the avoidance of doubt, any reinstatement of the default interest rate that would otherwise have taken effect on October 15, 2026 under Section 3 of the Second Amendment is hereby rescinded with effect from October 15, 2026, and no default interest has accrued or shall accrue on any amount outstanding under the Note for any period up to and including January 15, 2027. This limited waiver does not otherwise modify, supersede, or terminate Section 6(a) of the Original Note, which shall remain in full force and effect. If the Company fails to pay the Final Installment, together with all accrued and unpaid interest, in full on or before the Extended Maturity Date (January 15, 2027), then the waiver set forth in this Section 3 shall cease to apply, and the fifteen percent (15%) per annum default interest rate under Section 6(a) of the Original Note shall be reinstated and enforceable in full on all amounts then outstanding from and after January 16, 2027 until paid, in addition to all other rights and remedies of the Holder under the Original Note. The parties acknowledge and agree that any Event of Default arising solely from the failure to pay the Final Installment on May 31, 2026, September 1, 2026 or October 15, 2026 is hereby waived, such waiver being conditioned upon payment of all amounts due in full on or before the Extended Maturity Date. 4. Application of Payments. Consistent with Section 2(c) of the Original Note, all payments shall be applied first to accrued and unpaid interest and then to principal. 5. Amendment of Other Provisions. Wherever necessary, all other terms of the Note are hereby amended to be consistent with the terms of this Amendment. Except as specifically set forth herein, the Note shall remain in full force and effect. 6. Representations and Warranties. (a) The Company represents and warrants that (i) after giving effect to this Amendment (including the waiver and cure set forth in Section 3), no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing under the Note, (ii) the execution and delivery of this Amendment have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action, and (iii) this Amendment constitutes the legal, valid and binding obligation of the Company, enforceable in accordance with its terms. (b) The Holder represents and warrants that it is the holder of the Note, that it has full power and authority to enter into this Amendment, and that no consent of any third party is required for the Holder to do so. 2 7. Governing Law; Venue. This Amendment shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal substantive laws of the State of Nevada, without regard to conflict of law principles. The exclusive venue of any action arising under or in connection with this Amendment shall be the state or federal courts located in Clark County, Nevada. 8. Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. This Amendment may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by facsimile, email, or electronic signature (e.g., DocuSign) shall be as effective as delivery of an original executed counterpart. 9. Entire Agreement. This Amendment, together with the Note, constitutes the entire understanding of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings, written or oral, including any prior separate extension arrangements with respect to portions of the Final Installment. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned have executed this Amendment as of the Effective Date. COMPANY: Stewards Inc. Signature /s/ Katy Murless Print Name: Katy Murless Title: Chief Financial Officer Date: 11/11/2026 (To be signed by a duly authorized officer of the Company.) HOLDER: FAVO Holdings, LLC By its members / owners: Vincent Napolitano - Member (65%) /s/ Vincent Napolitano Signature Date: 11/11/2026 Shaun Quin - Member (35%) /s/ Shaun Quin Signature Date: 11/11/2026 3

text: EX-10.1 2 vor-ex10_1.htm EX-10.1 EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 THIS WARRANT AND THE SHARES OF COMMON STOCK ISSUABLE UPON THE EXERCISE OF THIS WARRANT (THE “SECURITIES”) HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “SECURITIES ACT”), OR THE SECURITIES LAWS OF ANY STATE OF THE UNITED STATES. THE SECURITIES HAVE BEEN ACQUIRED FOR INVESTMENT AND MAY NOT BE SOLD, TRANSFERRED OR ASSIGNED UNLESS (I) SUCH SECURITIES HAVE BEEN REGISTERED FOR SALE PURSUANT TO THE SECURITIES ACT, (II) SUCH SECURITIES MAY BE SOLD PURSUANT TO RULE 144 UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT, (III) THE COMPANY HAS RECEIVED AN OPINION OF COUNSEL REASONABLY SATISFACTORY TO IT THAT SUCH TRANSFER MAY LAWFULLY BE MADE WITHOUT REGISTRATION UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT, OR (IV) THE SECURITIES ARE TRANSFERRED WITHOUT CONSIDERATION TO AN AFFILIATE OF SUCH HOLDER OR A CUSTODIAL NOMINEE (WHICH FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT SHALL REQUIRE NEITHER CONSENT NOR THE DELIVERY OF AN OPINION). PRE-FUNDED WARRANT TO PURCHASE COMMON STOCK Number of Shares: 2,300,000 (subject to adjustment) Warrant No. A-1 Original Issue Date: November 12, 2026 Vor Biopharma Inc. , a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”), hereby certifies that, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, RemeGen Co., Ltd., or its registered assigns (the “ Holder ”), is entitled, subject to the terms set forth below, to purchase from the Company up to a total of 2,300,000 shares of common stock, $0.0001 par value per share (the “ Common Stock ”), of the Company (each such share, a “ Warrant Share ” and all such shares, the “ Warrant Shares ”) at an exercise price per share equal to $0.0001 (the “ Exercise Price ”), in each case as adjusted from time to time as provided in Section 9 , upon surrender of this Pre-Funded Warrant to Purchase Common Stock (including any Warrants to Purchase Common Stock issued in exchange, transfer or replacement hereof, the “ Warrant ”) at any time and from time to time on or after the later of (i) the Original Issue Date and (ii) if required to be obtained by the Holder in order for the Holder to hold the Warrant Shares, receipt by such Holder of ODI Approval (as defined below) (such date, the “ Initial Exercise Date ”). This Warrant is issued pursuant to that certain Securities Purchase Agreement, dated as of 11, 2026, by and between the Holder and the Company. The Warrant is issued in partial consideration of the rights granted by the Holder to the Company under that certain Amended and Restated License Agreement, dated as of November 11, 2026, by and between the Holder and the Company (the “ License Agreement ”). 1. Definitions . For purposes of this Warrant, the following terms shall have the following meanings: “ Affiliate ” means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that, directly or indirectly through one or more intermediates, controls, is controlled by or is under common control with such Person. “ Attribution Parties ” means, collectively, the following Persons and entities: (i) any direct or indirect Affiliates of the Holder, (ii) any Person acting or who could be deemed to be acting as a Group together with the Holder or any Attribution Parties and (iii) any other Persons whose beneficial ownership of the Company’s Common Stock would or could be aggregated with the Holder’s and/or any other Attribution Parties for purposes of Section 13(d) or Section 16 of the Exchange Act. For clarity, the purpose of the foregoing is to subject collectively the Holder and all other Attribution Parties to the Maximum Percentage. “ Closing Sale Price ” means, for any security as of any date, the last trade price for such security on the Principal Trading Market for such security, as reported by Bloomberg Financial Markets, or, if such Principal Trading Market begins to operate on an extended hours basis and does not designate the last trade price, then the last trade price of such security prior to 4:00 P.M., New York City time, as reported by Bloomberg Financial Markets, or if the foregoing do not apply, the last trade price of such security in the over-the-counter market on the electronic bulletin board for such security as reported by Bloomberg Financial Markets. If the Closing Sale Price cannot be calculated for a security on a particular date on any of the foregoing bases, the Closing Sale Price of such security on such date shall be the fair market value as mutually determined by the Company and the Holder. All such determinations shall be appropriately adjusted for any stock dividend, stock split, stock combination or other similar transaction during the applicable calculation period. “ Commission ” means the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. “ Exchange Act ” means the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and all of the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder. “ Group ” shall have the meaning ascribed to it in Section 13(d) of the Exchange Act, and all related rules, regulations and jurisprudence. “ ODI Approval ” means the completion of the overseas direct investment filing and the obtaining of the relevant approval from the National Development and Reform Commission of the PRC and the Ministry of Commerce of the PRC and/or the competent local counterparts, as well as the obtaining of relevant approvals and consents from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the PRC or the related foreign exchange bank with respect to the acquisition of the Warrant Shares. “ Original Issue Date ” means the “Original Issue Date” set forth on the first page of this Warrant. “ Person ” means an individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, business trust, joint stock company, trust, unincorporated association, joint venture or any other entity or organization. “ PRC ” means People’s Republic of China (excluding, for the purposes of this Agreement, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macau Special Administrative Region, or Taiwan). 2 “ Principal Trading Market ” means the national securities exchange or other trading market on which the Common Stock is primarily listed on and quoted for trading, which, as of the Original Issue Date, shall be the Nasdaq Global Select Market. “ Securities Act ” means the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and all of the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder. “ Standard Settlement Period ” means the standard settlement period, expressed in a number of Trading Days, for the Principal Trading Market with respect to the Common Stock that is in effect on the date of delivery of an applicable Exercise Notice, which as of the Original Issue Date was “T+1.” “ Trading Day ” means any weekday on which the Principal Trading Market is normally open for trading. “ Transfer Agent ” means Computershare Trust Company, N.A., the Company’s transfer agent and registrar for the Common Stock, and any successor appointed in such capacity. 2. Issuance of Securities; Registration of Warrants . The Company shall register ownership of this Warrant, upon records to be maintained by the Company for that purpose (the “ Warrant Register ”), in the name of the record Holder (which shall include the initial Holder or, as the case may be, any assignee to which this Warrant is permissibly assigned hereunder) from time to time. The Company may deem and treat the registered Holder of this Warrant as the absolute owner hereof for the purpose of any exercise hereof or any distribution to the Holder, and for all other purposes, absent actual notice to the contrary. 3. Registration of Transfers . Subject to compliance with all applicable securities laws, the Company shall register the transfer of all or any portion of this Warrant in the Warrant Register, upon surrender of this Warrant, and payment for all applicable transfer taxes (if any). Upon any such registration or transfer, a new warrant to purchase Common Stock in substantially the form of this Warrant (any such new warrant, a “ New Warrant ”) evidencing the portion of this Warrant so transferred shall be issued to the transferee, and a New Warrant evidencing the remaining portion of this Warrant not so transferred, if any, shall be issued to the transferring Holder. The acceptance of the New Warrant by the transferee thereof shall be deemed the acceptance by such transferee of all of the rights and obligations in respect of the New Warrant that the Holder has in respect of this Warrant. The Company shall prepare, issue and deliver at the Company’s own expense any New Warrant under this Section 3 . Until due presentment for registration of transfer, the Company may treat the registered Holder hereof as the owner and holder for all purposes, and the Company shall not be affected by any notice to the contrary. 4. Exercise of Warrants . (a) All or any part of this Warrant shall be exercisable by the registered Holder in any manner permitted by this Warrant (including Section 11) at any time and from time to time on or after the Initial Exercise Date, and such rights shall not expire. (b) The Holder may exercise this Warrant by delivering to the Company (i) an exercise notice, in the form attached as Schedule 1 (the “ Exercise Notice ”), completed and duly 3 signed, and (ii) payment of the Exercise Price for the number of Warrant Shares as to which this Warrant is being exercised (which may take the form of a “cashless exercise” if so indicated in the Exercise Notice pursuant to Section 10 below), and the date on which the last of such items is delivered to the Company (as determined in accordance with the notice provisions hereof) is an “Exercise Date .” The Company shall not require an ink-original Notice of Exercise, nor shall any medallion guarantee (or other type of guarantee or notarization) of any Notice of Exercise be required by the Company. The Holder shall not be required to deliver the original Warrant in order to effect an exercise hereunder. Execution and delivery of the Exercise Notice shall have the same effect as cancellation of the original Warrant and issuance of a New Warrant evidencing the right to purchase the remaining number of Warrant Shares, if any. (c) The Holder and any assignee, by acceptance of this Warrant, acknowledge and agree that, by reason of the provisions of this section, following the purchase of a portion of the Warrant Shares hereunder, the number of Warrant Shares available for purchase hereunder at any given time may be less than the amount stated on the face hereof. 5. Delivery of Warrant Shares . (a) Upon exercise of this Warrant, the Company shall promptly (but in no event later than the number of Trading Days comprising the Standard Settlement Period following the Exercise Date), upon the request of the Holder, cause the Transfer Agent to credit such aggregate number of shares of Common Stock specified by the Holder in the Exercise Notice and to which the Holder is entitled pursuant to such exercise (the “ Exercise Shares ”) to (i) the Holder’s or its designee’s balance account with The Depository Trust Company (“ DTC ”) through its Deposit Withdrawal At Custodian system or (ii) in book-entry form via a direct registration system (“ DRS ”) maintained by or on behalf of the Transfer Agent, in each case, so long as either (A) there is an effective registration statement permitting the issuance of the Warrant Shares to or the resale of such Warrant Shares by the Holder or (B) the Exercise Shares are eligible for resale by the Holder without volume or manner-of-sale restrictions pursuant to Rule 144 promulgated under the Securities Act (assuming cashless exercise of this Warrant). If (A) and (B) above are not true, the Company shall cause the Transfer Agent to either (i) record the Exercise Shares in the name of the Holder or its designee on the certificates reflecting the Exercise Shares with an appropriate legend regarding restriction on transferability, which shall be issued and dispatched by overnight courier to the address as specified in the Exercise Notice, and on the Company’s share register or (ii) issue such Exercise Shares in the name of the Holder or its designee in restricted book-entry form in the Company’s share register. The Holder, or any Person so designated by the Holder to receive Warrant Shares, shall be deemed to have become the holder of record of such Warrant Shares as of the Exercise Date, irrespective of the date such Warrant Shares are credited to the Holder’s DTC account, the date of the book entry positions or the date of delivery of the certificates evidencing such Exercise Shares, as the case may be. (b) In addition to any other rights available to the Holder, if the Company fails to cause the Transfer Agent to deliver to the Holder or its designee Exercise Shares in the manner required pursuant to Section 5(a) within the Standard Settlement Period following the Exercise Date (other than a failure caused by incorrect or incomplete information provided by Holder to the Company) and the Holder or the Holder’s broker on its behalf purchases (in an open market transaction or otherwise) shares of Common Stock to deliver in satisfaction of a sale by the Holder 4 of the Warrant Shares which the Holder anticipated receiving upon such exercise (a “ Buy-In ”) but did not receive within the Standard Settlement Period, then the Company shall, within two Trading Days after the Holder’s request and in the Holder’s sole discretion, promptly honor its obligation to deliver to the Holder or its designee the Exercise Shares pursuant to Section 5(a) and pay cash to the Holder in an amount equal to the excess (if any) of the Holder’s total purchase price (including brokerage commissions, if any) for the shares of Common Stock so purchased in the Buy-In, less the product of (A) the number of shares of Common Stock purchased in the Buy-In, times (B) the Closing Sale Price of a share of Common Stock on the Exercise Date. AND QUANTUM DRONES CORPORATION Exhibit 10.1 FIRST AMENDMENT TO IP LICENSE AGREEMENT This Amendment (the “ Amendment ”) to the Intellectual Property License Agreement dated June 11, 2026 (the “ IP License Agreement ”), as assigned and assumed under the Assignment and Assumption Agreement (between Quantum Cyber N.V. and its wholly-owned subsidiary Quantum Drones Corporation), is now entered into as of November 6, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), by and between Project LightShift, Inc., a Florida corporation, with offices located at 4040 NE 2nd Avenue #7D, Miami, Florida 33137 (“ Licensor ” or “ PLS ”), and Quantum Drones Corporation, a Nevada corporation having its principal place of business at 200 Connecticut Ave., Suite 400, Norwalk, CT 06854 (“ Quantum ,” or “ Licensee ”). Licensor and Licensee are hereinafter individually referred to as a “ Party ,” and collectively referred to as the “ Parties .” RECITALS WHEREAS , the Parties have entered into the IP License Agreement related to the Licensed Technology, which includes quantum array technology, quantum antenna systems and related products and services integrated into or designed for unmanned aerial vehicles and drone platforms, patents and related trade secrets, know-how, technical data, designs, and other proprietary information. WHEREAS , Licensee is prepared to commit substantial resources to develop a working prototype and further development, manufacturing scale-up, patent protection and commercialization of the Licensed Technology within the Field of Use as set forth herein while expressly preserving Licensor’s rights outside the Field of Use and providing Licensor additional consideration; NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the foregoing premises and the mutual covenants and obligations set forth in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties, intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows: ARTICLE I - INTRODUCTION 1.1 Definitions . In this Amendment, all capitalized terms shall have the definitions adopted in the IP License Agreement. 1.2 Schedule I of the IP License Agreement is amended as attached hereto to include all current Licensed Patents to which Licensee holds a license. ARTICLE 2 - AMENDMENTS TO THE LICENSE AGREEMENT 2.1 The “Field of Use” and “Licensed Products” definitions are amended and restated in their entirety to read as follows: “Field of Use” means the development, manufacture, integration, commercialization, marketing, sale, deployment, operation and support of Licensed Products solely for use in connection with (a) unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned aircraft systems, drones and related unmanned aerial platforms (collectively, “UAS”), and (b) unmanned surface vessels (“USVs”), unmanned underwater vehicles (“UUVs”), and related unmanned maritime or undersea platforms (collectively, “Unmanned Maritime Systems,” and together with UAS, “Licensed Unmanned Systems”), whether for defense, national security applications, homeland security, law enforcement, public safety, emergency response, border protection, critical infrastructure protection, or other governmental security applications. Within the Field of Use, Licensed Products may employ any functionality enabled by the Licensed Technology in connection with Licensed Unmanned Systems. The Field of Use also includes ground-based, airborne, maritime, subsea or space-based products, systems or infrastructure to the extent designed and deployed primarily to detect, identify, track, communicate with, control, navigate, counter, power, support or provide services to Licensed Unmanned Systems (“Dedicated Unmanned Systems Infrastructure”). For the avoidance of doubt, the Field of Use excludes general-purpose and standalone applications of the Licensed Technology in energy generation or infrastructure, electric grids, stationary power systems, terrestrial telecommunications, satellite or space systems, computing or data centers, consumer electronics, automotive or manned transportation, ground robotics, manned maritime vessels, shipping or maritime infrastructure, subsea infrastructure, medical applications or industrial systems. A product or system in any of these categories is included only to the extent that it qualifies as Dedicated Unmanned Systems Infrastructure and serves the defense, national security, homeland security, law enforcement, public safety, emergency response, border protection, critical infrastructure protection or other governmental security applications expressly described above. Incidental or secondary use of a product or service in connection with Licensed Unmanned Systems shall not bring such product or service within the Field of Use. All rights to the Licensed Technology outside the Field of Use are expressly reserved by Licensor, and no rights outside the Field of Use shall arise by implication, estoppel or otherwise. 1 of 7 “Licensed Products” means all quantum photonic array technology (including antenna systems) and related products and services integrated into or designed for UASs, USVs, UUVs, and Unmanned Maritime Systems, the manufacture, use, offer for sale, sale, importation, or other exploitation of which utilizes or incorporates any Licensed Technology, in each case regardless of form factor, configuration, branding, or generation. 2.2. Amendments to Section 2.1 and Section 2.3. Section 2.1 shall be replaced, superseded, amended and restated by the following. Section 2.1. Scope of Grant. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement (including Licensee’s satisfaction of any remaining funding obligations set forth in Section 4), Licensor, on behalf of itself and its Affiliates, hereby grants to Licensee and its designated Affiliates during the Term an exclusive (even as to Licensor), irrevocable right and license to the Licensed Technology and all associated Intellectual Property Rights to make, have made, use, offer to sell, sell, import, and otherwise exploit Licensed Products solely within the Field of Use in the Territory. For the avoidance of doubt, all rights to the Licensed Technology outside the Field of Use are expressly reserved by Licensor. No license or other right outside the Field of Use is granted by implication, estoppel or otherwise. Section 2.3 shall be replaced, superseded, amended and restated by the following. Section 2.3. Sublicensing. Licensee has the right in its sole discretion to grant sublicenses through multiple tiers under the Licensed Technology within the Licensed Field of Use. The terms of any sublicense to a third party, including consideration of any sublicense, shall be provided to Licensor within 30 days after execution of any such sublicense. If Licensee or its Affiliates grants to a third party a license, sublicense, or other right to make, use, sell, or otherwise exploit the Licensed Technology, then sales and other dispositions by such sublicensee shall not constitute Commercial Sales. In lieu of any Royalty on such sublicensee’s sales, Licensee shall pay to Licensor ten percent (10%) of the Sublicense Income actually received by Licensee or its Affiliates. The term “ Sublicense Income ” shall for purposes of this Section 2.3 have the same meaning, mutatis mutandis, as set forth in Section 4.7 below for Licensor. 2.3. Amendment to Section 4.7. Section 4.7 shall be replaced, superseded, amended and restated by the following. (a) Based on the Cash Consideration and Consideration Shares provided to Licensor under this Article 4, the inability of Licensor to provide a working or successful Prototype, and the significant additional research & development funds Licensee will continue to provide to pursue development of a successful Prototype, the rights granted to Licensee under Article 2 shall remain in effect until termination of the IP License Agreement. (b) In any circumstance where Licensor successfully commercializes a product or service related to or embodying any Improvement developed after the Effective Date of this Agreement (whether or not a successful Prototype is demonstrated), Licensor shall pay to Licensee a royalty equal to ten percent (10%) of Net Revenues received by Licensor or its Affiliates (“ Royalty ”) that are attributable to Commercial Sales of such products or services related to or embodying such Improvement. Royalties shall be calculated and paid on a quarterly basis, within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter, accompanied by a written report setting forth in reasonable detail the calculation of such Royalty. The Parties hereby agree such royalty will be reasonable to compensate Licensee for its Cash Payment, other consideration provided to Licensor under this Agreement, and other development funding of the Licensed Technology. 2 of 7 (c) Sublicensing. Royalties shall accrue only on Net Revenues actually received by Licensor or its Affiliates in cash or cash equivalents. No Royalty shall accrue on invoiced amounts, receivables, or other amounts until actually collected. If Licensor pays a Royalty on amounts that are later written off as uncollectible, refunded, or otherwise not retained by Licensor or its Affiliates, Licensor may credit the Royalty paid on such amounts against Royalties subsequently payable. If any Commercial Sale is made for consideration other than cash, Net Revenues for such Commercial Sale shall be the fair market value of such consideration, as reasonably determined in good faith by Licensor. If Licensor or any of its Affiliates grants to a third party a license, sublicense, or other right to make, use, sell, or otherwise exploit any Improvement (a “Sublicensee”), then sales and other dispositions by such Sublicensee shall not constitute Commercial Sales. In lieu of any Royalty on such Sublicensee’s sales, Licensor shall pay to Licensee ten percent (10%) of the Sublicense Income actually received by Licensor or its Affiliates. “Sublicense Income” means royalties, license fees, and other amounts actually received by Licensor or its Affiliates from a Sublicensee as consideration for the grant of rights to an Improvement. Sublicense Income excludes amounts received: (i) as payment for equity or debt securities of Licensor or its Affiliates, at or below fair market value; (ii) as loans or other debt financing; (iii) as funding for, or reimbursement of, research, development, engineering, testing, or regulatory certification activities; (iv) as reimbursement of costs of prosecuting, maintaining, or enforcing intellectual property rights; and (v) as payment for products or services supplied by Licensor or its Affiliates, which shall be treated as Commercial Sales to the extent otherwise included. If a Sublicensee receives rights to both an Improvement and other technology for a single payment, Sublicense Income shall be reasonably allocated to the Improvement in good faith by Licensor. Sublicense Income shall be reported in the written reports required under Section 4.7(d). Amounts paid on Sublicense Income shall constitute Royalties for all purposes of this Agreement, including the Royalty Cap under Section 4.7(e). (d) Royalty Reports. Each written report delivered under Section 4.7(b) shall set forth, for each calendar month within the applicable calendar quarter: (i) revenues from the Licensed Technology and service offerings; (ii) the gross amounts received and each deduction taken in calculating Net Revenues; and (iii) the resulting Net Revenues and the calculation of the Royalty due for such quarter. Licensee shall have the right to audit any such written report, and the books and records of Licensor and its Affiliates relating to such report upon delivery to Licensor of written notice accompanied by written evidence supporting the basis for the audit. Any audit shall be conducted during Licensor’s normal business hours, upon no less than fifteen (15) days’ prior written notice, and by Licensee or an independent accountant designated by Licensee and reasonably acceptable to Licensor. All costs and expenses of any audit shall be borne by Licensee. Licensee may conduct no more than two (2) audits in any calendar year. If an audit reveals that Licensor has underpaid any Royalty, Licensor shall pay the amount of such underpayment to Licensee within thirty (30) days following receipt of the audit results. If the underpayment is by more than 5% of the audited Royalties paid, then Licensor shall bear all costs and expenses of such audit. 3 of 7 (e) Royalty Initiation. Licensor’s obligation to pay Royalties under Section 4.7(b) shall commence upon the first Commercial Sale of a product or service related to or embodying an Improvement (the “First Commercial Sale”). That obligation shall terminate automatically upon termination of this IP License Agreement. Licensor shall pay any such accrued Royalties, together with the final written report required under Section 4.7(d), within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter. Licensee’s audit rights under Section 4.7(d) shall survive expiration of the IP License Agreement for a period of twelve (12) months following such expiration or termination. 2.4. Royalties From Licensee to Licensor. After Licensee recovers an amount equal to four (4) times its Development Costs (as defined below) incurred to achieve commercial sales of Licensed Products, Licensee will pay to Licensor a royalty payment equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the cost attributable to a quantum photonic array used in the completed commercial sale of a Licensed Product or related service to an end-use customer, where payment is actually received by Licensor or its Affiliates from such customer (“ Licensee Royalty ”). Licensee Royalties owed to Licensor will be reduced, when applicable, by an amount to ensure the cost of the Licensed Products does not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the total sale price of the applicable “end-use product”. “End-use products” are anticipated to include UASs, USVs, UUVs, and Unmanned Maritime Systems. Licensee Royalties shall be calculated and paid on a quarterly basis, within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter, accompanied by a written report setting forth in reasonable detail the calculation of such Licensee Royalty. Licensee Royalties to Licensor will not be owed to Licensor in the event the end-user cost does not provide for sufficient profit margin in the benefit of the licensee after recovering manufacturing costs. “ Development Costs ,” as used herein, means (i) all funding for, or reimbursement of, research, development, engineering, testing, or regulatory certification activities, including without limitation the Cash Consideration paid under the IP License Agreement and all further development costs leading to a successful Prototype; (ii) all up-front costs of goods sold before commercial manufacturing is initiated; and (iii) all costs for preparing, prosecuting, maintaining, or enforcing intellectual property rights (including legal fees associated therewith). Licensee will provide Royalty Reports to Licensor, and Licensor will have audit rights, mutatis mutandis, as set forth above in Section 2.3. Licensee Royalty obligations will also termination automatically upon any expiration or termination of this IP License Agreement. 2.5. Licensee Field Improvements. Licensee may own Licensed-Unmanned-Systems-specific integration, packaging, mounting, interface, configuration, application-design or customer-specific implementation technology conceived and developed solely by Licensee that does not constitute a Licensed Technology (each, a “ Licensee Field Improvement ”). To the extent any Licensee Field Improvement is capable of use outside the Field of Use, Licensee hereby grants to Licensor and its designated Affiliates during the Term of the IP License Agreement a worldwide, fully paid-up license to use, reproduce, modify, make, have made, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise exploit such Licensee Field Improvement outside the Field of Use on the Royalty basis set forth in Section 2.3 (replacing Section 4.7) above. 4 of 7 2.6. No Technology Wide Expansion. For the avoidance of doubt, the term Field of Use as set forth in Sections 2.1 and 2.2 of this Amendment shall not be construed as granting Licensee rights to the Licensed Technology on a technology-wide, function-wide or general commercial application basis outside the Field of Use. Nothing in this First Amendment grants Licensee any right in any separate technology or intellectual property of Licensor or any of its Affiliates that is not already included under the Licensed Technology merely because such technology is interoperable with, complementary to or used alongside a Licensed Product. 2.7. Effect of Termination. The following provisions shall be added to the end of Section 13.3 of the IP License Agreement. In the event of a termination by Licensor under Section 13.2(b) as a result of a breach by Licensee, all rights, grants and licenses granted hereunder shall automatically terminate and Licensee shall have no further right to the Licensed Technology. In such event, Licensee shall return to Licensor all technical information, documentation know-how and other material provided by Licensor to Licensee and shall cease the use of any Licensed Technology unless otherwise agreed by Licensor. ARTICLE 3- MISCELLANEOUS (a) Ratification. Except as specifically amended by this Amendment, the IP License Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and is hereby ratified and confirmed. This Amendment shall be construed as one with the Agreement, and the IP License Agreement shall, where the context requires, be read and construed throughout so as to incorporate this Amendment. All documents executed in connection with the IP License Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and are hereby ratified and confirmed with respect to the IP License Agreement, as amended by this Amendment. (b) Entire Agreement. This Amendment, together with the IP License Agreement, supersedes all prior agreements and understandings, written or oral, between Licensor and Licensee with respect to the subject matter of this Amendment. (c) Counterparts. This Amendment may be executed in any number of counterparts, all of which, when taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument and the parties to this Amendment may execute this Amendment by signing any such counterpart. Signature pages may be detached from multiple separate counterparts and attached to a single counterpart so that all signatures are physically attached to the same documents (d) Effective Date. This Amendment shall be deemed effective upon execution by both Parties. 5 of 7 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, each Party has caused its name to be hereunto subscribed, by its duly authorized officer as of the date indicated above.
